vocabulary.example: Le centre accueille les nouveaux arrivants du lundi au vendredi.
vocabulary.note: Ends in `-ir` but takes the `-er` endings: `j’accueille`.

vocabulary.example: Deux lignes de métro desservent ce secteur depuis l’an dernier.
vocabulary.note: Transit meaning first; it also means to clear a table.

vocabulary.example: Une ligne d’autobus supplémentaire reliera le quartier à la gare.
vocabulary.note: Feminine noun phrase; the gender comes from `ligne`.

vocabulary.example: Un virement automatique évite les retards de paiement du loyer.
vocabulary.note: Masculine noun; `faire un virement` is the usual verb phrase.

vocabulary.example: Nous craignons que le délai soit trop court pour rassembler les pièces.
vocabulary.note: Plural stem in `-gn-`; the participle is `craint`.

practice.prompt: Conjugate for `je` and `nous`: `nettoyer`, `craindre`, `connaître`, `suivre`. Then give the future of `envoyer`, `voir`, and `prévoir` for `je`.
practice.hint: All four present-tense pairs change their written stem; the future of `prévoir` does not follow `voir`.
practice.answer: je nettoie / nous nettoyons ; je crains / nous craignons ; je connais / nous connaissons ; je suis / nous suivons. J’enverrai ; je verrai ; je prévoirai.

takeaways: Silent ending equals `i` in `-oyer` and `-uyer`; `-ayer` allows both spellings.
`-indre` gives `-gn-` in the plural and `-aître` doubles the `s`.
`Rire` and `courir` keep their stems in the present; their endings change.
`Envoyer` has the future `enverr-`, `voir` has `verr-`, but `prévoir` keeps `prévoir-`.
keywords: dire, redire, prédire, interdire, médire, contredire, maudire
conduire, produire, cuire, traduire, construire, détruire, séduire, déduire

lessons.title: Le passé récent
lessons.summary: The recent past is the fixed pattern `venir de` plus infinitive: it states that an action has just happened. Only `venir` is conjugated, and `de` is obligatory. In the present it means has just; in the imperfect (`je venais de`) it means had just. Do not confuse it with `venir` plus infinitive without `de`, which expresses movement in order to do something.
objectives: Conjugate `venir` correctly for each subject.
Keep `de` before the infinitive in every person.
Distinguish the recent past from `venir` used as a movement verb.

sections.title: Core concept
paragraphs: The recent past expresses that something has just happened through a multiword verb construction, called a verbal periphrasis. `Venir` carries the person and the tense, `de` links the two verbs, and the second verb stays in the infinitive: `Je viens de terminer`, `Nous venons de recevoir`, `Le ministère vient d’annoncer`. `De` elides to `d’` before a vowel.

Two contrasts matter. First, tense: `je viens de déposer` means I have just submitted, while `je venais de déposer` means I had just submitted and situates the action before another past moment. Second, structure: without `de`, `venir` plus infinitive keeps its movement meaning, so `Je viens terminer la réunion` means I am coming in order to finish the meeting. A time expression can specify how recent the action is: `Je viens de terminer la réunion, il y a deux minutes`. With an explicit time marker, `J’ai terminé la réunion il y a deux minutes` is a concise alternative, not a grammatical correction.
points: Conjugate `venir` for the subject: `je viens`, `nous venons`, `ils viennent`.
Insert `de` or `d’` before the infinitive, without exception.
Leave the second verb in the infinitive, never in a participle.
Use the imperfect `venais de` for had just.
Read `venir` plus bare infinitive as movement, not as recent past.

examples.french: Je viens de terminer mon entrevue d’embauche.
examples.english: I have just finished my job interview.
examples.note: Present of venir plus de plus infinitive.

examples.french: Le ministère vient d’annoncer une nouvelle mesure de soutien.
examples.english: The ministry has just announced a new support measure.
examples.note: « De » elides before a vowel.

examples.french: Nous venons de recevoir votre demande de logement.
examples.english: We have just received your housing application.
examples.note: Only venir changes for the subject.

examples.french: Je venais de déposer le dossier quand le guichet a fermé.
examples.english: I had just submitted the file when the counter closed.
examples.note: Imperfect of venir for an action just completed in the past.

examples.french: Je viens terminer la réunion avec vous, puis je repars.
examples.english: I am coming to finish the meeting with you, then I am leaving again.
examples.note: Without « de », venir keeps its movement meaning.

examples.french: Je viens de terminer la réunion, il y a deux minutes.
examples.english: I just finished the meeting, two minutes ago.
examples.note: The time expression specifies how recent the event is; using the compound past would be a more concise alternative.

mistakes.avoid: Je vient de terminer la réunion.
mistakes.prefer: Je viens de terminer la réunion.
mistakes.why: With `je`, the present of `venir` is `viens`, not the third-person form `vient`.

mistakes.avoid: Nous venons de reçu votre demande.
mistakes.prefer: Nous venons de recevoir votre demande.
mistakes.why: The recent past takes an infinitive, never a past participle.

vocabulary.example: Elle vient de recevoir sa confirmation d’inscription.
vocabulary.note: Fixed pattern; only `venir` is conjugated and `de` is obligatory.

vocabulary.example: La ville vient d’annoncer la gratuité des transports le dimanche.
vocabulary.note: `-cer` verb: cedilla before `a` and `o`.

vocabulary.example: Une réunion d’information vient de se terminer dans la grande salle.
vocabulary.note: Feminine noun; `se réunir` is the related verb.

vocabulary.example: Une mesure de soutien temporaire aide les familles à faible revenu.
vocabulary.note: Feminine noun phrase; the gender comes from `mesure`.

practice.prompt: Say in French that the service has just closed, and that it had just closed when you arrived.
practice.hint: Present of `venir` first, then the imperfect.
practice.answer: Le service vient de fermer. Le service venait de fermer quand je suis arrivé.

takeaways: `Venir de` plus infinitive equals has just.
`Venais de` plus infinitive equals had just.
Dropping `de` turns the sentence back into movement.

lessons.title: Commencer une action ou être en train de la faire
lessons.summary: The simple present can describe an ongoing action. Être en train de plus infinitive emphasises progress at a present, past, future, or recurring reference moment; se mettre à plus infinitive highlights the moment an action begins. Do not create an English-style continuous tense with être plus a present participle.
objectives: Build `être en train de` plus infinitive in the present, the imperfect, and the future.
Explain why French cannot translate *I am filling in* with a present participle.
Distinguish an ordinary habit from an action in progress at a recurring reference moment.
Use se mettre à for an action beginning, rather than already in progress.

sections.title: Core concept
paragraphs: English marks a continuous aspect inside the verb: *I fill in* versus *I am filling in*. French has no such tense. The simple present covers both readings, and `Je remplis le formulaire` is already the normal translation of *I am filling in the form*. When you need to insist that the action is under way at the moment you are describing, French adds a separate phrase instead of changing the verb: `être en train de` plus an infinitive. `Je suis en train de remplir le formulaire` states explicitly that the action is happening right now.

Three details make the construction reliable. Only `être` carries person and tense, so the second verb stays in the infinitive. `Je suis remplissant` cannot express the English continuous. `De` belongs to the fixed phrase. Finally, the tense of `être` sets the reference point: now (`Le conseiller est en train de vérifier votre dossier`), a past moment (`Elle était en train de garer la voiture quand l’agent est arrivé`), or a future moment (`À dix heures, nous serons en train de passer l’entretien`). Repetition is compatible with this focus: `Tous les matins à huit heures, je suis en train de déjeuner` describes what is in progress at that time each day. For a plain habit, `Tous les matins, je prends l’autobus` is the simpler choice.
points: Conjugate only `être`; leave the second verb in the infinitive.
Keep `de` or `d’` between `en train` and the infinitive.
Use the present of `être` for an action under way now.
Use the imperfect of `être` for an action under way at a past moment, typically interrupted by a compound past.
Use the simple present for an unmarked habit; the progressive can describe what is under way at a recurring moment.
Remember that the plain present already translates the English continuous when no insistence is needed.

examples.french: Je suis en train de remplir ma demande de logement social.
examples.english: I am in the middle of filling in my social housing application.
examples.note: Present of « être »; the action is under way at the moment of speaking.

examples.french: Nous sommes en train de faire traduire les documents pour l’inscription.
examples.english: We are in the middle of having the documents translated for the registration.
examples.note: The infinitive after « de » can itself be a causative « faire » construction.

examples.french: Elle était en train de garer la voiture quand l’agent est arrivé.
examples.english: She was in the middle of parking the car when the officer arrived.
examples.note: Imperfect of « être » for the ongoing action, compound past for the interruption.

examples.french: Le conseiller est en train de vérifier votre dossier ; veuillez patienter quelques minutes.
examples.english: The adviser is checking your file right now; please wait a few minutes.
examples.note: Typical counter formula justifying a wait.

examples.french: À dix heures, nous serons en train de passer l’entretien d’embauche.
examples.english: At ten o’clock we will be in the middle of the job interview.
examples.note: Future of « être » for an action under way at a coming moment.

examples.french: Tous les matins, je prends l’autobus de sept heures pour aller au travail.
examples.english: Every morning I take the seven o’clock bus to go to work.
examples.note: The simple present states the habit without focusing on an action in progress.

examples.french: Tous les matins à huit heures, je suis en train de déjeuner.
examples.english: Every morning at eight, I am in the middle of eating breakfast.
examples.note: The action is in progress at the same reference time each day. Déjeuner means breakfast here, as in Canadian French; in France it usually means lunch.

mistakes.avoid: Je suis remplissant le formulaire en ligne.
mistakes.prefer: Je suis en train de remplir le formulaire en ligne.
mistakes.why: French cannot place a present participle after `être` to build a continuous tense; the fixed phrase `être en train de` plus infinitive does that job.

mistakes.avoid: À huit heures, je suis en train de prends l’autobus.
mistakes.prefer: À huit heures, je suis en train de prendre l’autobus.
mistakes.why: The verb after `de` must be the infinitive `prendre`, not the conjugated form `prends`.

mistakes.avoid: Nous sommes en train remplir le dossier.
mistakes.prefer: Nous sommes en train de remplir le dossier.
mistakes.why: `De` belongs to the fixed phrase and is never omitted before the infinitive.

sections.title: Se mettre à: the moment an action begins
paragraphs: Se mettre à plus infinitive means begin or start doing something. It highlights the onset, whereas être en train de highlights an action already under way. Compare Elle s’est mise à chanter (she started singing) and Elle était en train de chanter (she was singing at that moment).

Conjugate se mettre and keep the following verb in the infinitive: je me mets à lire, nous nous mettons à lire. Compound tenses use être; in this construction, mis agrees with the subject: elle s’est mise, ils se sont mis, elles se sont mises.
points: Se mettre à: onset; être en train de: progress at a reference moment.
Keep à and match the reflexive pronoun to the subject.

examples.french: Quand la musique a commencé, elle s’est mise à chanter.
examples.english: When the music began, she started singing.
examples.note: The construction identifies the beginning of her action.

examples.french: Elle était en train de chanter quand nous sommes entrés.
examples.english: She was singing when we came in.
examples.note: Here the singing was already in progress.

examples.french: Après la réunion, nous nous mettons à rédiger le compte rendu.
examples.english: After the meeting, we start drafting the minutes.
examples.note: Nous nous mettons à is followed by the infinitive rédiger.

mistakes.avoid: Elle s’est mis à chanter.
mistakes.prefer: Elle s’est mise à chanter.
mistakes.why: Mise agrees with elle in se mettre à.

mistakes.avoid: Nous nous mettons de rédiger le compte rendu.
mistakes.prefer: Nous nous mettons à rédiger le compte rendu.
mistakes.why: The construction requires à before the infinitive.

vocabulary.english: to be in the middle of doing
vocabulary.example: Je suis en train de préparer les pièces justificatives demandées.
vocabulary.note: Only `être` is conjugated; the following verb stays in the infinitive.

vocabulary.example: Une demande de logement peut prendre plusieurs mois à être traitée.
vocabulary.note: Feminine noun phrase; the gender comes from `demande`.

vocabulary.example: Veuillez patienter dans la salle d’attente jusqu’à l’appel de votre nom.
vocabulary.note: More formal than `attendre` and used with no object.

vocabulary.example: Il est interdit de garer sa voiture devant l’entrée de l’immeuble.
vocabulary.note: `Se garer` is the pronominal form used when no object is named.

vocabulary.example: Un entretien d’embauche de quarante-cinq minutes est prévu demain.
vocabulary.note: Masculine noun phrase; `une entrevue` is the usual Canadian equivalent.

practice.prompt: Rewrite twice: « Je remplis le formulaire. » — once to insist that it is happening right now, once to say it was happening when the counter closed.
practice.hint: Only the tense of `être` changes; the infinitive stays.
practice.answer: Je suis en train de remplir le formulaire. / J’étais en train de remplir le formulaire quand le guichet a fermé.

takeaways: French has no continuous tense; `être en train de` plus infinitive supplies the meaning.
The tense of `être` sets the moment; the second verb never changes.
Use the plain present for an ordinary habit; the progressive can focus on an action at a repeated reference moment.

lessons.title: La formation du passé composé
lessons.summary: The compound past combines a present-tense auxiliary with a past participle. Most verbs take avoir; pronominal verbs take être. Learn the common non-pronominal être verbs individually, not as a universal movement rule. Some verbs change auxiliary with their construction or meaning. Non-pronominal être verbs agree with the subject; pronominal agreement needs a separate object check.
objectives: Select the auxiliary from the verb type and from the presence of a direct object.
Build the past participle of regular and frequent irregular verbs.
Apply subject agreement with non-pronominal être verbs and recognise common pronominal exceptions.

sections.title: Core concept
paragraphs: An auxiliary is a helping verb. The passé composé combines present-tense `avoir` or `être` with a past participle, the form seen in `j’ai parlé` (I spoke). Regular `-er` verbs have participles in `-é`; the `finir` family has `-i`, and the `attendre` family has `-u`. Other `-ir` and `-re` verbs need checking: `venir → venu`, `prendre → pris`. Most verbs use `avoir`, including movement verbs such as `marcher` and `courir`.

Verbs used with a pronoun referring back to their subject are called pronominal verbs: `se laver`, `s’inscrire`. They use `être`. Common non-pronominal verbs using `être` include `aller`, `venir`, `arriver`, `partir`, `entrer`, `sortir`, `rentrer`, `rester`, `tomber`, `naître`, `mourir`, `devenir`, and `retourner`; learn their usual meanings with examples. `Monter`, `descendre`, and `passer` also commonly use `être` for a person's movement.

A direct object is attached to the verb without a preposition: `monter les cartons` (carry the boxes up). With direct objects, `monter`, `descendre`, `sortir`, `rentrer`, `passer`, and `retourner` use `avoir`: `Elle a monté les cartons`. Contrast `Elle est montée au troisième étage` (She went up to the third floor). This is a construction test, not a test of whether an object moves: `Elle a monté l’escalier` means she climbed the stairs. Without a direct object, meaning and usage can still matter: `Le prix a monté` (The price rose) is correct.

With non-pronominal `être` verbs, the participle agrees with the subject: `elle est arrivée`, `ils sont partis`, `elles sont restées`. With `avoir`, there is no subject agreement: `elles ont travaillé`; a preceding direct object can cause agreement: `les lettres qu’elles ont écrites` (the letters they wrote). Do not apply subject agreement blindly to pronominal verbs: `elles se sont lavées` (they washed themselves), but `elles se sont lavé les mains` (they washed their hands), because `les mains` is the direct object and follows the verb. `Elles se sont parlé` (they spoke to each other) stays unchanged because French has `parler à quelqu’un`, an indirect object. The agreement lesson develops these contrasts.
points: Pronominal verbs use être, but their participles do not all agree with the subject.
Learn which non-pronominal verbs use être; movement alone does not decide.
Add a direct object test for `monter`, `descendre`, `sortir`, `rentrer`, `passer`, `retourner`.
Agree with the subject for non-pronominal être verbs; check object roles in reflexive and reciprocal uses.
Leave the participle unchanged after `avoir` unless a direct object precedes it.

examples.french: Elle est arrivée au Canada avec sa famille l’an dernier.
examples.english: She arrived in Canada with her family last year.
examples.note: « Arriver » takes être, and the participle agrees with the subject.

examples.french: Nous nous sommes inscrits à un programme de formation professionnelle.
examples.english: We enrolled in a professional training program.
examples.note: Every reflexive verb takes être.

examples.french: La technicienne est montée au troisième étage pour réparer le réseau.
examples.english: The technician went up to the third floor to repair the network.
examples.note: « Monter » with no object: auxiliary être.

examples.french: Elle a monté les cartons au troisième étage avant la réunion.
examples.english: She carried the boxes up to the third floor before the meeting.
examples.note: The same verb with a direct object: auxiliary avoir, no agreement.

examples.french: Nous avons attendu la réponse pendant six semaines.
examples.english: We waited for the answer for six weeks.
examples.note: Default auxiliary avoir with a regular -re participle.

mistakes.avoid: Elle a allé à la clinique ce matin.
mistakes.prefer: Elle est allée à la clinique ce matin.
mistakes.why: `Aller` belongs to the `être` list, and its participle then agrees with the subject.

mistakes.avoid: Elle est montée les dossiers au deuxième étage.
mistakes.prefer: Elle a monté les dossiers au deuxième étage.
mistakes.why: With a direct object, `monter` switches to the auxiliary `avoir`.

vocabulary.english: to enrol in, to register for
vocabulary.example: Nous nous sommes inscrits à un cours de français avancé.
vocabulary.note: Reflexive, so the auxiliary is always `être`; participle `inscrit`.

vocabulary.english: to go up; to carry up
vocabulary.example: Elle est montée à l’étage, puis elle a monté les dossiers.
vocabulary.note: Auxiliary `être` alone, `avoir` with a direct object.

vocabulary.example: Une inscription tardive a tout de même été acceptée par le centre.
vocabulary.note: Feminine noun; the ending -tion is a feminine hint.

vocabulary.example: Un étage supplémentaire a été construit au-dessus du magasin.
vocabulary.note: Masculine noun; the ground floor is `le rez-de-chaussée`.

practice.prompt: Put into the compound past: « Elle (sortir) à midi. » and « Elle (sortir) les documents du classeur. »
practice.hint: The second sentence has a direct object.
practice.answer: Elle est sortie à midi. Elle a sorti les documents du classeur.

takeaways: Pronominal verbs use être; learn the usual auxiliary of other verbs with their construction.
Monter, descendre, sortir, rentrer, passer, and retourner use avoir with direct objects.
Non-pronominal être verbs agree with their subject. Pronominal verbs need a separate agreement check.

lessons.title: Les familles de participes passés irréguliers
lessons.summary: Many irregular past participles follow useful ending patterns: `-u` in `voulu`, `reçu`, `tenu`; `-is` in `pris`, `mis`, `compris`; `-it` in `dit`, `écrit`, `conduit`; `-ert` in `ouvert`, `offert`, `couvert`; and `-int` in `peint`, `joint`, `atteint`. These are not the only endings: `ri`, `fui`, `lui`, and `nui` end in `-i`. A known base often helps predict a derivative, but auxiliary choice and agreement must be checked separately.
objectives: Sort a new irregular verb into the right participle family.
Derive compound verbs from the base verb you already know.
Reuse each participle immediately in a compound tense.

sections.title: Core concept
paragraphs: A past participle is the verb form used with an auxiliary, as `reçu` in `nous avons reçu`. Its basic form may acquire agreement endings in other constructions. Many irregular participles cluster into useful families: `prendre` gives `pris`, and the related `apprendre`, `comprendre`, and `reprendre` give `appris`, `compris`, and `repris`. The five main patterns illustrated here are a learning aid, not an exhaustive list.

The same logic applies elsewhere: `tenir` gives `tenu`, so `obtenir` gives `obtenu` and `maintenir` gives `maintenu`; `écrire` gives `écrit`, so `décrire` gives `décrit` and `inscrire` gives `inscrit`; `ouvrir` gives `ouvert`, so `couvrir` gives `couvert` and `découvrir` gives `découvert`. Choosing the family does not settle the auxiliary or the agreement, which are decided separately.

Many verbs in `-uire` have participles in `-uit`: `conduit`, `traduit`, `construit`, `détruit`, `produit`, `introduit`, `réduit`. This is not universal: `luire` gives `lui`, and `nuire` gives `nui`. Check the construction separately from the ending. In ordinary active uses, these verbs take `avoir`: `Elle a conduit jusqu’à Laval`, even though driving involves movement. Pronominal forms take `être`: `Elle s’est conduite correctement` means she behaved correctly. The passive also uses `être`: `Elle est conduite à la clinique` means she is being driven to the clinic. Neither construction is an error.
points: Identify the base verb hidden inside a prefixed verb.
Look for common patterns in `-u`, `-is`, `-it`, `-ert`, and `-int`, while recognising other endings such as `-i`.
Use the base verb to help learn derivatives, and check their actual forms.
Check the auxiliary separately; the family says nothing about it.
Write each new participle inside a full compound-past sentence.
Use `avoir` in `elle a conduit`; distinguish the pronominal `elle s’est conduite` and the passive `elle est conduite`.
Many `-uire` participles end in `-uit`, but learn exceptions such as `lui` and `nui`.

examples.french: Nous avons reçu la confirmation de notre rendez-vous ce matin.
examples.english: We received confirmation of our appointment this morning.
examples.note: « Recevoir » belongs to the -u family.

examples.french: Avez-vous ouvert le courriel envoyé par le ministère ?
examples.english: Did you open the email sent by the ministry?
examples.note: « Ouvrir » belongs to the -ert family.

examples.french: J’ai pris rendez-vous et j’ai compris toute la procédure.
examples.english: I made an appointment and understood the whole procedure.
examples.note: « Prendre » gives pris, so « comprendre » gives compris.

examples.french: Elle a obtenu son permis et elle a écrit une lettre de remerciement.
examples.english: She obtained her permit and wrote a thank-you letter.
examples.note: The `tenir` and `écrire` families give `obtenu` and `écrit`.

examples.french: Le service a atteint son objectif et a produit un rapport détaillé.
examples.english: The department reached its target and produced a detailed report.
examples.note: « Atteindre » is in the -int family, « produire » in the -it family.

examples.french: Elle a conduit jusqu’à Laval pour l’entretien, et j’ai traduit les documents en anglais.
examples.english: She drove to Laval for the interview, and I translated the documents into English.
examples.note: « Conduire » takes « avoir » despite expressing movement.

examples.french: Nous avons construit un dossier complet et nous avons réduit le délai de traitement.
examples.english: We built a complete file and we shortened the processing time.
examples.note: Same family, same auxiliary and same participle ending.

examples.french: Ce retard a nui au projet, mais la responsable s’est conduite avec professionnalisme.
examples.english: This delay harmed the project, but the manager behaved professionally.
examples.note: « Nuire » gives « nui »; pronominal « se conduire » takes être.

mistakes.avoid: J’ai comprendu la consigne du premier coup.
mistakes.prefer: J’ai compris la consigne du premier coup.
mistakes.why: `Comprendre` follows `prendre`, whose participle is `pris`.

mistakes.avoid: Elle a ouvri le dossier hier après-midi.
mistakes.prefer: Elle a ouvert le dossier hier après-midi.
mistakes.why: `Ouvrir` belongs to the `-ert` family.

mistakes.avoid: Elle a conduis jusqu’à Laval pour son entretien.
mistakes.prefer: Elle a conduit jusqu’à Laval pour son entretien.
mistakes.why: The past participle is `conduit`; `conduis` is a present-tense form.

mistakes.avoid: J’ai traduis les documents demandés par le ministère.
mistakes.prefer: J’ai traduit les documents demandés par le ministère.
mistakes.why: `Traduis` is a present-tense form; the past participle of `traduire` is `traduit`.

vocabulary.example: J’ai compris la consigne après une deuxième lecture.
vocabulary.note: Participle `compris`, from the `prendre` family.

vocabulary.example: Le programme a atteint son objectif de participation.
vocabulary.note: Participle `atteint`, from the `-indre` family.

vocabulary.example: Une confirmation écrite a été reçue le lendemain matin.
vocabulary.note: Feminine noun; frequent in administrative correspondence.

vocabulary.example: Un courriel officiel a confirmé la date du rendez-vous.
vocabulary.note: Masculine noun; the term recommended in formal Quebec French. Un mail is common in France.

vocabulary.example: Elle a conduit deux heures pour se rendre à la clinique.
vocabulary.note: Active `conduire` takes `avoir` here; distinguish pronominal `se conduire` and the passive, which use `être`.

practice.prompt: Give the past participle: `apprendre`, `découvrir`, `maintenir`, `décrire`.
practice.hint: Each one belongs to a family you already know.
practice.answer: appris, découvert, maintenu, décrit

takeaways: Five useful ending patterns cover many irregular participles, not all of them.
A prefix often preserves a participle pattern: comprendre follows prendre; check unfamiliar derivatives.
The family gives the form, never the auxiliary.
Many `-uire` verbs give `-uit`, but `luire` gives `lui` and `nuire` gives `nui`; auxiliary choice depends on the construction.

lessons.title: L’imparfait
lessons.summary: The imperfect describes a past situation from the inside: background, description, a state, an action in progress, or a repeated habit. Build it from the present `nous` form minus `-ons`, then add `-ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient`. `Être` is the only verb with an irregular stem, `ét-`. Verbs in `-cer` write `ç` and verbs in `-ger` keep `e` before endings starting with `a`: `je commençais`, `il neigeait`.
objectives: Derive the imperfect stem from the present `nous` form.
Choose the imperfect for habit, description, and ongoing background.
Apply the spelling adjustments of `-cer` and `-ger` verbs.

sections.title: Core concept
paragraphs: The imperfect presents a past situation without marking its beginning or end. It therefore covers four everyday uses: a repeated habit (`je faisais du bénévolat chaque semaine`), a description or state (`il faisait froid`), an action in progress interrupted by another (`je travaillais quand la connexion est tombée`), and a past viewpoint in reported speech (`il a dit qu’il voulait déménager`).

Take the present `nous` form, remove `-ons`, and add `-ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient`: `je finissais, tu finissais, il finissait, nous finissions, vous finissiez, ils finissaient`. `Nous prenons` gives `je prenais`; `nous faisons` gives `je faisais`. `Être` uses the exceptional stem `ét-`: `j’étais`, `nous étions`. Verbs normally used only with impersonal `il` need their own reference form: `il fallait` (it was necessary), `il pleuvait` (it was raining).

Two spelling families protect pronunciation: `-cer` verbs write `ç` before `a` (`je commençais` but `nous commencions`), and `-ger` verbs keep `e` before `a` (`il neigeait`, `je mangeais`, but `nous mangions`). Keep the ending's `i` even after a stem ending in `i`: `nous étudiions`, `vous étudiiez`.

Repeated actions are not automatically imperfect. Use it to describe an open-ended habit: `À cette époque, je nageais chaque matin` (At that time, I used to swim every morning). The passé composé can sum up repetitions within a completed period: `Pendant mes vacances, j’ai nagé chaque matin` (During my holiday, I swam every morning). The viewpoint, not the word `chaque`, decides.
points: Start from the present `nous` form, not from the infinitive.
Use the imperfect for a habit, a description, or an action in progress.
Remember the single irregular stem: `ét-` for `être`.
Write `ç` in `-cer` verbs before `-ais`, `-ait`, `-aient`.
Keep the `e` in `-ger` verbs before those same endings.

examples.french: Je travaillais à distance lorsque la connexion est tombée en panne.
examples.english: I was working remotely when the connection went down.
examples.note: Imperfect for the ongoing action, compound past for the interruption.

examples.french: Quand j’étais étudiant, je faisais du bénévolat chaque semaine.
examples.english: When I was a student, I volunteered every week.
examples.note: Irregular stem ét- and a repeated habit.

examples.french: Il faisait froid et les routes étaient glissantes ce matin-là.
examples.english: It was cold and the roads were slippery that morning.
examples.note: Description and background.

examples.french: Je commençais mon bénévolat et il neigeait déjà sur la ville.
examples.english: I was beginning my volunteer work and it was already snowing over the city.
examples.note: `-cer` takes ç and `-ger` keeps e before -ait.

examples.french: Nous commencions toujours la réunion par un tour de table.
examples.english: We always started the meeting with a round of introductions.
examples.note: No ç before -ions, because the ending does not start with a.

mistakes.avoid: Quand j’étais petit, je nageait chaque matin.
mistakes.prefer: Quand j’étais petit, je nageais chaque matin.
mistakes.why: The imperfect ending for je is -ais, not the third-person -ait. Here the imperfect describes a childhood habit; a passé composé could instead summarise repetitions over a bounded period.

mistakes.avoid: Je commencais mon stage en septembre.
mistakes.prefer: Je commençais mon stage en septembre.
mistakes.why: A `-cer` verb needs the cedilla before an ending starting with `a`.

vocabulary.example: Je faisais du bénévolat dans une banque alimentaire chaque samedi.
vocabulary.note: Fixed expression; `un bénévole` is the person.

vocabulary.example: Je commençais toujours par relire la consigne.
vocabulary.note: `-cer` verb: cedilla before `a` and `o`.

vocabulary.example: Une habitude quotidienne rend les progrès plus réguliers.
vocabulary.note: Feminine noun; `avoir l’habitude de` means to be used to.

vocabulary.example: Une connexion instable a interrompu l’entrevue en ligne.
vocabulary.note: Feminine noun; the ending -ion is a feminine hint.

practice.prompt: Put into the imperfect for `je` and `nous`: `manger`, `placer`, `être`.
practice.hint: The `nous` forms lose the spelling adjustment.
practice.answer: je mangeais / nous mangions, je plaçais / nous placions, j’étais / nous étions

takeaways: Stem from the present `nous` form; only `être` is irregular.
Habit, description, ongoing action, past viewpoint.
`ç` and `e` appear only before endings starting with `a`.

lessons.title: Le choix d’un temps du passé
lessons.summary: The compound past presents bounded events; the imperfect supplies background or habits. The pluperfect places an event before another past reference point. For literary recognition, distinguish the simple past, the past anterior formed with a simple-past auxiliary, and indicative fut versus subjunctive fût.
objectives: Separate narrative events from background information.
Form and place the pluperfect for an earlier past event.
Recognise the simple past, past anterior, and literary fût without making them everyday production targets.

sections.title: Core concept
paragraphs: A useful narrative pattern is to put completed events that advance the story in the passé composé and background in the imperfect. `Je préparais mon entrevue` sets the scene; `quand la responsable m’a appelé` moves the story forward. This is a viewpoint choice, not a rule based on the verb's meaning: `Il a fait froid toute la semaine` (It was cold all week) presents weather over a completed period, while `Il faisait froid` (It was cold) describes the setting.

Use the pluperfect, `le plus-que-parfait`, to look back from a past reference point to an earlier event. It uses the imperfect of the auxiliary plus a past participle, with the same auxiliary and agreement rules as the passé composé: `j’avais déposé ma demande`, `elle était déjà partie`, `nous nous étions inscrits`. Not every pair of past events needs it: `J’ai signé, puis je suis parti` narrates two events in sequence. The pluperfect also follows conditional `si` for an unreal past condition. The simple past, `le passé simple`, commonly replaces the passé composé in literary narration: `il entra`, `elle fut`, `ils prirent`. Recognition is the priority here, although writers can use these forms in their own literary narratives.
points: Ask whether the verb advances the story or paints the scene.
Use the compound past for the event and the imperfect for the setting.
Use the pluperfect for whatever happened before the main past event.
Build the pluperfect with the imperfect of `avoir` or `être` plus a participle.
Recognise `il entra` or `elle fut` as literary narration, not as everyday speech.
Je devais can describe an obligation or intended action without saying whether it happened. J’ai dû often presents a past necessity, or a deduction: j’ai dû oublier (I must have forgotten).

examples.french: Je préparais mon entrevue quand la responsable m’a appelé.
examples.english: I was preparing for my interview when the manager called me.
examples.note: Background in the imperfect, event in the compound past.

examples.french: J’ai déménagé au Québec il y a quelques semaines.
examples.english: I moved to Quebec a few weeks ago.
examples.note: A single bounded event.

examples.french: Quand je suis arrivé au guichet, j’avais déjà rempli le formulaire en ligne.
examples.english: When I arrived at the counter, I had already completed the form online.
examples.note: Pluperfect for the action completed before the main past event.

examples.french: Elle était partie avant que la décision soit annoncée.
examples.english: She had left before the decision was announced.
examples.note: Pluperfect with the auxiliary être and subject agreement.

examples.french: Il entra dans la salle, salua l’assemblée et s’assit.
examples.english: He entered the room, greeted the assembly, and sat down.
examples.note: Simple past: recognise it in written narration.

examples.french: Je devais envoyer le dossier hier, mais j’ai dû reporter l’envoi au lundi suivant.
examples.english: I was supposed to send the file yesterday, but I had to postpone it to the following Monday.
examples.note: « Je devais » is the unfulfilled plan; « j’ai dû » is what actually happened.

mistakes.avoid: Quand je suis arrivé, j’ai déjà envoyé le dossier la veille.
mistakes.prefer: Quand je suis arrivé, j’avais déjà envoyé le dossier la veille.
mistakes.why: Déjà and la veille locate the sending before the past arrival. The pluperfect makes that backward-looking relationship explicit.

mistakes.avoid: Hier, il a fais la demande et il a obtenu une réponse immédiate.
mistakes.prefer: Hier, il a fait la demande et il a obtenu une réponse immédiate.
mistakes.why: After a, use the past participle fait, not the present form fais. Both passé composé forms present completed events; faisait would instead present making the request as ongoing background.

mistakes.avoid: J’ai dois envoyer le dossier hier, mais je ne l’ai pas fait.
mistakes.prefer: Je devais envoyer le dossier hier, mais je ne l’ai pas fait.
mistakes.why: J’ai dois is not a compound tense: dois is a present form, not the participle dû. Je devais describes the past obligation; mais je ne l’ai pas fait tells us it was not fulfilled. Neither tense should be treated as a universal guarantee that an obligation was met.

sections.title: Reading recognition: passé antérieur and fût
paragraphs: The passé antérieur combines a simple-past auxiliary with a participle: j’eus parlé, elle fut arrivée. In literary narration, it often marks completion just before another simple-past event, especially after dès que, quand, or après que. Recognise it as an earlier completed action; ordinary narration generally uses compound-past or pluperfect constructions instead.

Fût, with a circumflex, is different: it is the third-person singular imperfect subjunctive of être. In literary Bien qu’il fût fatigué, the mood comes from bien que. Modern usage normally has bien qu’il soit fatigué, even with a past main event. Fut without a circumflex is indicative simple past. Neither spelling is simply a more elegant substitute for the other.
points: Past anterior: simple-past avoir/être + participle.
Distinguish indicative fut from literary subjunctive fût.

examples.french: Dès qu’elle eut signé la lettre, elle quitta le bureau.
examples.english: As soon as she had signed the letter, she left the office.
examples.note: Eut signé is past anterior; quitta advances the literary narrative.

examples.french: Quand les voyageuses furent arrivées, le guide ouvrit la porte.
examples.english: When the travellers had arrived, the guide opened the door.
examples.note: Être supplies furent; arrivées agrees with the feminine plural subject.

examples.french: Bien qu’il fût fatigué, il poursuivit sa route.
examples.english: Although he was tired, he continued on his way.
examples.note: Literary imperfect subjunctive; a modern equivalent is Bien qu’il soit fatigué, il a poursuivi sa route.

mistakes.avoid: Il entra et fût accueilli par le guide.
mistakes.prefer: Il entra et fut accueilli par le guide.
mistakes.why: This narrative indicative is fut, without a circumflex.

mistakes.avoid: Quand elles furent arrivé, le guide ouvrit la porte.
mistakes.prefer: Quand elles furent arrivées, le guide ouvrit la porte.
mistakes.why: The past anterior retains ordinary agreement with être.

vocabulary.example: Nous avions déménagé deux fois avant de trouver ce logement.
vocabulary.note: `-ger` verb; keeps the `e` before `a` and `o`.

vocabulary.example: J’avais déposé ma demande avant la date limite.
vocabulary.note: Regular `-er` verb; `déposer un dossier` is standard administrative usage.

vocabulary.example: Une entrevue d’embauche m’attendait le lendemain matin.
vocabulary.note: Feminine noun used in Canada; `un entretien` in France.

vocabulary.example: Un guichet unique regroupe désormais toutes les démarches.
vocabulary.note: Masculine noun; `un guichet automatique` is a cash machine.

vocabulary.english: to have to, to be supposed to
vocabulary.example: Nous devions commencer à neuf heures, mais la salle n’était pas libre.
vocabulary.note: Imperfect `je devais` = was supposed to; compound past `j’ai dû` = had to, or must have.

practice.prompt: Complete with the right past tense: « Quand elle (arriver) à la réunion, tout le monde (partir) déjà. »
practice.hint: The second verb happened before the first.
practice.answer: Quand elle est arrivée à la réunion, tout le monde était déjà parti.

takeaways: Completed-event versus background is a useful viewpoint contrast, not a fixed classification of verbs.
Use the pluperfect to look back from a past reference point: imperfect auxiliary plus participle.
Prioritise recognising the simple past; it remains available for literary writing.
keywords: choosing a past tense and the pluperfect
passé antérieur, passé simple, plus-que-parfait, imparfait du subjonctif, fut, fût

lessons.title: Les formes du futur
lessons.summary: The simple future adds `-ai, -as, -a, -ons, -ez, -ont` to a regular infinitive, dropping the final e of an -re infinitive. Learn irregular stems such as ser-, aur-, fer-, ir-, viendr-, pourr-, voudr-, verr-, devr-, saur-, and tiendr-. The near future uses present aller plus an infinitive; neither form is restricted to a fixed distance into the future.
objectives: Build the simple future from a regular or irregular stem.
Choose between the simple future and the near future.
Use the future after time conjunctions where English uses the present.

sections.title: Core concept
paragraphs: The simple future is a single word: infinitive plus ending. `Parler` gives `je parlerai`, `finir` gives `je finirai`, and `attendre` drops its `e` to give `j’attendrai`. The endings are the present forms of `avoir` reduced, which is why every simple future ends in `-ai`, `-as`, `-a`, `-ons`, `-ez`, `-ont`. Irregular verbs change only the stem, never the endings.

The near future, aller plus infinitive, often connects a plan or prediction to the present situation and is common in speech: Nous allons présenter notre projet demain. It need not mean immediately; the simple future can also describe something only minutes away. In the negative, surround conjugated aller: La ville ne va pas construire de logements. In careful future narration, time clauses with quand, lorsque, dès que, and aussitôt que normally use a future tense where English uses the present.

Keep these irregular stem pairs together: être → ser-, avoir → aur-, faire → fer-, aller → ir-, venir → viendr-, pouvoir → pourr-, vouloir → voudr-, voir → verr-, devoir → devr-. Add savoir → saur- and tenir → tiendr-: je saurai, nous saurons; je tiendrai, vous tiendrez. The endings remain regular. Tenir can mean hold or keep, including tenir une promesse (to keep a promise). The spelling-family lesson separately covers envoyer → enverr- and prévoir → prévoir-.
points: Add the endings straight to the infinitive for regular verbs.
Drop the final `e` of an `-re` infinitive before adding the ending.
Learn each irregular future stem with its infinitive, including savoir → saur- and tenir → tiendr-.
Normally place ne… pas around conjugated aller to negate a near-future statement.
In careful future narration, clauses with quand, lorsque, and dès que normally use a future tense where English uses the present.

examples.french: Nous réduirons nos déchets grâce à ce nouveau programme municipal.
examples.english: We will reduce our waste thanks to this new municipal program.
examples.note: Regular formation on an -re infinitive.

examples.french: Nous serons prêts et nous aurons tous les documents demandés.
examples.english: We will be ready and we will have all the requested documents.
examples.note: Irregular stems ser- and aur-.

examples.french: Je prendrai rendez-vous dès que le bureau ouvrira.
examples.english: I will make an appointment as soon as the office opens.
examples.note: French uses the future in both clauses after « dès que ».

examples.french: Nous allons présenter notre projet devant le comité demain.
examples.english: We are going to present our project to the committee tomorrow.
examples.note: Near future for a planned action.

examples.french: La ville ne va pas construire de logements sur ce terrain.
examples.english: The city is not going to build housing on this land.
examples.note: The negative surrounds « va », and « des » becomes « de ».

examples.french: Je saurai demain si ma demande a été acceptée.
examples.english: I will know tomorrow whether my application has been accepted.
examples.note: Saurai comes from savoir. Here si means whether, not if in a conditional hypothesis.

examples.french: Nous tiendrons notre promesse et vous tiendrez les résidents informés.
examples.english: We will keep our promise, and you will keep the residents informed.
examples.note: Both forms use tiendr-. A promise is une promesse (f.).

examples.french: Quand vous saurez la date, nous maintiendrons ou modifierons la réservation.
examples.english: When you know the date, we will keep or change the reservation.
examples.note: Savoir uses saur-; maintenir follows tenir with maintiendr-.

mistakes.avoid: Quand j’arrivera au Canada, je chercherai un emploi.
mistakes.prefer: Quand j’arriverai au Canada, je chercherai un emploi.
mistakes.why: The je ending is -ai, not -a. For a future arrival, careful French normally uses the future after quand, unlike English when I arrive. A present with future meaning can occur in conversation; it is not inherently ungrammatical.

mistakes.avoid: Il ne va pas venir pas à la réunion.
mistakes.prefer: Il ne va pas venir à la réunion.
mistakes.why: A single ne… pas pair around va negates this statement; the second pas is redundant.

mistakes.avoid: Je savoirai la réponse demain.
mistakes.prefer: Je saurai la réponse demain.
mistakes.why: Savoir has the irregular future stem saur-, not savoir-.

mistakes.avoid: Nous tenirons notre promesse.
mistakes.prefer: Nous tiendrons notre promesse.
mistakes.why: Tenir has the future stem tiendr-.

vocabulary.example: Nous réduirons la consommation d’énergie de vingt pour cent.
vocabulary.note: `-re` verb; the future drops the final `e`: `je réduirai`.

vocabulary.example: Vous pourrez suivre votre demande en ligne dès lundi.
vocabulary.note: Irregular future stem `pourr-`.

vocabulary.example: Un déchet mal trié complique tout le processus de recyclage.
vocabulary.note: Masculine noun, usually used in the plural: `les déchets`.

vocabulary.example: Un terrain municipal sera transformé en parc de quartier.
vocabulary.note: Masculine noun; also means ground or field.

practice.prompt: Put into the simple future: « Je (faire) la demande dès que je (pouvoir). »
practice.hint: Both verbs have irregular stems, and French keeps the future after `dès que`.
practice.answer: Je ferai la demande dès que je pourrai.

takeaways: Infinitive plus `-ai, -as, -a, -ons, -ez, -ont`, with `-re` losing its `e`.
Savoir → saur- and tenir → tiendr- take the same future endings as the other irregular stems.
For a future event, French normally uses a future tense after quand where English uses the present.
keywords: savoir, tenir, saur-, tiendr-, futur simple, futur proche

lessons.title: Le conditionnel, les hypothèses et les conditions
lessons.summary: The present conditional uses a future stem with imperfect endings; the past conditional uses aurais/serais and a past participle. Besides hypothetical results and politeness, these forms express future from a past viewpoint, past regret, and unconfirmed reports. Condition connectors have different constructions: si and sauf si take indicative forms, au cas où takes the conditional, and à condition que, pourvu que, and à moins que take the subjunctive.
objectives: Form the present and past conditional from the future stem.
Match each type of condition to its pair of tenses.
Use the conditional for politeness, future-in-the-past, regret, and unconfirmed present or past reports.
Choose a condition connector by its complement type and required mood.

sections.title: Core concept
paragraphs: The conditional is built on the future stem, so any verb you can put in the future you can put in the conditional: `je serai` gives `je serais`, `il faudra` gives `il faudrait`. The endings are those of the imperfect. The past conditional adds a participle to a conditional auxiliary: `je serais parti`, `j’aurais postulé`.

Three common patterns provide a starting point. An open present or future possibility uses `si` plus present, with a present, future, or imperative result: `Si vous avez des questions, appelez le service`. A more hypothetical situation now or later uses `si` plus imperfect with the present conditional: `Si j’avais plus d’expérience, je postulerais`. An unreal past situation uses `si` plus pluperfect with the past conditional: `Si j’avais connu ce programme, je me serais inscrit plus tôt`. Outside `si` clauses, the conditional alone softens a request (`Je voudrais un rendez-vous`) or marks unverified information (`Le service fermerait plus tôt`).

These are not the only combinations. Match each clause to its own time: `Si j’avais accepté ce poste, je travaillerais maintenant à Lyon` (If I had accepted that job, I would now be working in Lyon) combines a past condition with a present result. An open question about a past fact can use the passé composé: `Si vous avez déjà payé, ignorez ce rappel` (If you have already paid, disregard this reminder).
points: Take the future stem and add `-ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient`.
Keep the present after `si` when the condition is realistic.
Use the imperfect after `si` for a present or future hypothesis.
Use the pluperfect after `si` for a past that did not happen.
Use `je voudrais`, `pourriez-vous`, `j’aimerais` for polite requests.

examples.french: Si la ville améliore le service, davantage de résidents prendront le bus.
examples.english: If the city improves the service, more residents will take the bus.
examples.note: Real possibility: present plus future.

examples.french: Si vous avez des questions, appelez le service d’aide aux nouveaux arrivants.
examples.english: If you have questions, call the newcomer support service.
examples.note: Present plus imperative.

examples.french: Si j’avais plus d’expérience, je postulerais à ce poste.
examples.english: If I had more experience, I would apply for this position.
examples.note: Present hypothesis: imperfect plus present conditional.

examples.french: Si j’avais connu ce programme, je me serais inscrit plus tôt.
examples.english: If I had known about this program, I would have enrolled earlier.
examples.note: Past counterfactual: pluperfect plus past conditional.

examples.french: Je voudrais prendre rendez-vous avec une conseillère en emploi.
examples.english: I would like to make an appointment with an employment adviser.
examples.note: Conditional alone for a polite request.

mistakes.avoid: Si tu travaillerais, tu réussirais l’examen.
mistakes.prefer: Si tu travaillais, tu réussirais l’examen.
mistakes.why: In this conditional hypothesis, si takes the imperfect, not the conditional. Interrogative si meaning whether is a different construction.

mistakes.avoid: Si j’aurais su, je serais venu plus tôt.
mistakes.prefer: Si j’avais su, je serais venu plus tôt.
mistakes.why: A past counterfactual requires the pluperfect after `si`.

sections.title: Future-in-the-past, regret, and unconfirmed reports
paragraphs: A conditional can express time rather than uncertainty. In Lundi, elle a annoncé qu’elle viendrait mardi, the visit is future relative to Monday’s announcement. The direct words Je viendrai mardi become elle a annoncé qu’elle viendrait mardi when the report adopts that past viewpoint. This does not mean she was unsure. Reporting with que does not automatically select the subjunctive; the meaning and reporting verb govern the construction.

The past conditional is a conditional auxiliary plus a participle: j’aurais dû, elle serait venue. J’aurais dû vérifier expresses regret or criticism about something that should have been done. J’aurais aimé participer expresses an unrealised wish. Choose avoir or être as in other compound tenses and apply the usual agreement rules.

Journalistic conditional forms distance the speaker from information that has not been confirmed. Le directeur serait absent reports a possible present state; le directeur aurait démissionné reports a possible completed resignation. A source phrase such as selon le journal clarifies whose information this is. These are not hypothetical if-clauses, and they do not establish that the report is false.
points: Use the conditional to locate a future event from a past reporting viewpoint.
Use aurais dû plus infinitive for a past action that should have been done.
Distinguish unconfirmed present states from unconfirmed completed events.

examples.french: Lundi, la conseillère a annoncé qu’elle nous rappellerait mardi.
examples.english: On Monday, the adviser announced that she would call us back on Tuesday.
examples.note: Rappellerait is future from the announcement’s past viewpoint.

examples.french: Il a expliqué qu’il était malade et qu’il reviendrait la semaine suivante.
examples.english: He explained that he was ill and would return the following week.
examples.note: The report combines an indicative background state with future-in-the-past, not an automatic subjunctive after que.

examples.french: J’aurais dû vérifier l’adresse avant d’envoyer la lettre.
examples.english: I should have checked the address before sending the letter.
examples.note: Aurais dû expresses past regret; une adresse (f.) is an address.

examples.french: Nous aurions aimé participer, mais les inscriptions étaient closes.
examples.english: We would have liked to take part, but registration had closed.
examples.note: The past conditional presents an unrealised wish.

examples.french: Selon le journal local, le directeur aurait démissionné hier; son adjointe serait actuellement absente.
examples.english: According to the local newspaper, the director reportedly resigned yesterday; his deputy is reportedly absent at present.
examples.note: Aurait démissionné reports an unconfirmed past event; serait absente an unconfirmed current state.

mistakes.avoid: Elle a annoncé qu’elle venirait mardi.
mistakes.prefer: Elle a annoncé qu’elle viendrait mardi.
mistakes.why: Venir uses the future/conditional stem viendr-.

mistakes.avoid: Selon le journal, le directeur aurait démissionner.
mistakes.prefer: Selon le journal, le directeur aurait démissionné.
mistakes.why: The past conditional needs the participle démissionné after aurait.

sections.title: Conditions beyond si: clauses, infinitives, and nouns
paragraphs: À condition que introduces an explicit requirement with the subjunctive: à condition que vous fournissiez une preuve. Pourvu que also takes the subjunctive and often presents the condition as sufficient: pourvu que le dossier soit complet. Used alone, Pourvu qu’il arrive à temps! can instead express a wish: Let’s hope he arrives in time. À condition de takes an infinitive whose actor is normally understood from the main clause: Vous pouvez entrer à condition de présenter votre carte.

Au cas où introduces a precautionary possibility and takes the conditional in standard usage: au cas où le bureau serait fermé. En cas de takes a noun phrase rather than a finite clause: en cas de fermeture. Neither construction asserts that the problem will happen.

À moins que gives an exception with the subjunctive. Formal French may add an optional ne that does not negate the clause, called expletive ne: à moins qu’il (ne) pleuve means unless it rains with or without ne. Sauf si also introduces an exception, but uses the indicative: sauf s’il pleut. Sinon links an alternative consequence, meaning otherwise: Partez maintenant, sinon vous raterez le train. It does not select a special mood by itself.

Do not extend the conditional-si rule to every word si. In Je me demande si elle viendra and Je voudrais savoir si vous pourriez m’aider, si means whether and introduces an indirect question. Future and conditional forms are possible there.
points: Clause with subjunctive: à condition que, pourvu que, à moins que.
Clause with conditional: au cas où.
Conditional clause with indicative: si, sauf si.
Infinitive: à condition de; noun phrase: en cas de; alternative consequence: sinon.

examples.french: La demande sera acceptée à condition que vous fournissiez une preuve de résidence.
examples.english: The application will be accepted provided that you supply proof of residence.
examples.note: An explicit requirement selects the subjunctive fournissiez.

examples.french: Vous pouvez utiliser la salle à condition de la laisser propre.
examples.english: You may use the room provided you leave it clean.
examples.note: The infinitive laisser has the same understood actor as pouvez.

examples.french: Nous maintiendrons la rencontre pourvu que la salle soit disponible.
examples.english: We will keep the meeting scheduled as long as the room is available.
examples.note: Pourvu que introduces a sufficient condition with the subjunctive.

examples.french: Prenez une copie papier au cas où le portail serait inaccessible.
examples.english: Take a paper copy in case the website is unavailable.
examples.note: Au cas où takes conditional serait; une copie (f.) is a copy and un portail (m.) a website portal.

examples.french: En cas de panne, appelez ce numéro; sinon, utilisez le formulaire en ligne.
examples.english: If there is a breakdown, call this number; otherwise, use the online form.
examples.note: En cas de introduces the noun une panne (f.); sinon links the alternative instruction.

examples.french: Nous sortirons à moins qu’il ne pleuve. Autrement dit, nous sortirons sauf s’il pleut.
examples.english: We will go out unless it rains. In other words, we will go out except if it rains.
examples.note: Pleuve is subjunctive after à moins que; pleut is indicative after sauf si. The first ne is expletive.

examples.french: Je voudrais savoir si vous pourriez déplacer le rendez-vous.
examples.english: I would like to know whether you could move the appointment.
examples.note: Interrogative si means whether; the conditional is grammatical here.

mistakes.avoid: Prenez une copie au cas où le portail soit inaccessible.
mistakes.prefer: Prenez une copie au cas où le portail serait inaccessible.
mistakes.why: Standard au cas où selects the conditional, not the subjunctive.

mistakes.avoid: Nous viendrons pourvu que la salle est libre.
mistakes.prefer: Nous viendrons pourvu que la salle soit libre.
mistakes.why: Pourvu que selects the subjunctive soit.

mistakes.avoid: Vous pouvez entrer à condition de vous présentez votre carte.
mistakes.prefer: Vous pouvez entrer à condition de présenter votre carte.
mistakes.why: À condition de takes an infinitive. To name a subject in a finite clause, use à condition que vous présentiez.

vocabulary.example: Si la ville améliorait le service, davantage de résidents prendraient le bus.
vocabulary.note: Regular `-er` verb; the conditional stem is the full infinitive.

vocabulary.example: Je voudrais obtenir une attestation de résidence.
vocabulary.note: Conditional `je voudrais` is the standard polite request form.

vocabulary.example: Un délai de traitement plus court serait apprécié par tous les usagers.
vocabulary.note: Masculine noun phrase; the gender comes from `délai`.

vocabulary.example: Une hypothèse raisonnable mérite d’être vérifiée avant la conclusion.
vocabulary.note: Feminine noun beginning with a mute h.

practice.prompt: Complete: « Si le service (être) ouvert samedi, je (déposer) mon dossier ce week-end. »
practice.hint: Frame Saturday opening as hypothetical rather than as an open possibility: use imperfect plus conditional.
practice.answer: Si le service était ouvert samedi, je déposerais mon dossier ce week-end.

takeaways: Future stem plus imperfect endings equals the conditional.
Present with future, imperfect with present conditional, pluperfect with past conditional.
Conditional si differs from interrogative si meaning whether.
The conditional can locate a future event from a past viewpoint or mark regret and unconfirmed information.
Memorise each alternative condition connector with its complement and mood, not as an interchangeable synonym for si.
keywords: conditionnel passé, futur dans le passé, regret au passé, conditionnel journalistique
à condition que, pourvu que, à condition de, au cas où, en cas de, à moins que, sauf si, sinon

lessons.title: L’impératif et les pronoms
lessons.summary: The imperative exists only for `tu`, `nous`, and `vous`, and the subject pronoun is not written. Regular `-er` verbs drop the final `-s` in the `tu` form (`parle`, `remplis` for `-ir` verbs keeps it), but the `-s` returns before `y` and `en` (`vas-y`, `manges-en`). In an affirmative command, pronouns follow the verb with a hyphen and `me` becomes `moi`; in a negative command, they return to their usual place before the verb.
objectives: Form the three imperative persons, including irregular être and avoir.
Attach pronouns correctly in an affirmative command.
Restore the normal order in a negative command.

sections.title: Core concept
paragraphs: The imperative gives instructions, advice, or encouragement. Most forms correspond to present-indicative tu, nous, and vous without a written subject: Remplis le formulaire, Remplissons le formulaire, Remplissez le formulaire. Être and avoir are important exceptions, taught below. The tu imperative of -er verbs and aller has no final s: parle, va. Some -ir verbs with -e forms behave similarly: ouvre, offre. Other verbs retain s, as in finis and prends. An s is added before attached y or en for pronunciation: vas-y, manges-en.

Pronoun placement is the main difficulty. In an affirmative command the pronouns follow the verb, joined by hyphens, and the stressed forms `moi` and `toi` replace `me` and `te`: `Donnez-moi le formulaire`, `Envoyez-lui une copie`, `Asseyez-vous`. In a negative command everything returns to the ordinary pre-verbal order: `Ne le leur transmettez pas`, `Ne t’inquiète pas`. For a very formal written instruction, French often prefers `veuillez` plus an infinitive: `Veuillez signer le formulaire`.
points: For most verbs, use the present form without its subject; learn the irregular forms separately.
Drop the final `-s` in the `tu` form of `-er` verbs and of `aller`.
Add -s before attached y or en: vas-y, parles-en. Do not add it when the pronoun belongs to a following infinitive: Va en chercher (Go and get some), without a hyphen.
Attach pronouns after the verb with hyphens in an affirmative command, using `moi` and `toi`.
Put the pronouns back before the verb in a negative command.
Read product and safety notices as imperatives addressed to `vous`: `Agitez bien avant emploi`.

With two pronouns, put le/la/les before the person in an affirmative command: Donne-le-moi (Give it to me), Envoyez-le-leur (Send it to them). Negatives use ordinary order: Ne me le donne pas, Ne le leur envoyez pas.
Before en, moi and toi become m’ and t’: Donne-m’en (Give me some), Va-t’en (Go away). The hyphen comes before m’/t’, not between the apostrophe and en.

examples.french: Prépare tes documents, puis vas-y sans attendre.
examples.english: Get your documents ready, then go ahead without waiting.
examples.note: « Prépare » loses the -s; « vas-y » gets it back before y.

examples.french: Donnez-moi le formulaire, s’il vous plaît.
examples.english: Give me the form, please.
examples.note: Affirmative command: pronoun after the verb, « me » becomes « moi ».

examples.french: Envoyez-lui une copie du dossier avant vendredi.
examples.english: Send him or her a copy of the file before Friday.
examples.note: Indirect pronoun joined by a hyphen.

examples.french: Ne le leur transmettez pas avant la vérification finale.
examples.english: Do not send it to them before the final check.
examples.note: Negative command: ordinary pre-verbal order returns.

examples.french: Veuillez signer le formulaire et le retourner par courriel.
examples.english: Please sign the form and return it by email.
examples.note: Formal written instruction with « veuillez » plus infinitive.

examples.french: Agitez bien avant emploi et conservez le flacon à l’abri de la lumière.
examples.english: Shake well before use and keep the bottle away from light.
examples.note: Product notices use the « vous » imperative with no subject pronoun.

mistakes.avoid: Me donnez le formulaire, s’il vous plaît.
mistakes.prefer: Donnez-moi le formulaire, s’il vous plaît.
mistakes.why: In an affirmative command the pronoun follows the verb and `me` becomes `moi`.

mistakes.avoid: Ne donnez-le pas avant la vérification.
mistakes.prefer: Ne le donnez pas avant la vérification.
mistakes.why: A negative command restores the ordinary order, with the pronoun before the verb.

sections.title: Être and avoir: six imperative forms to know
paragraphs: Do not obtain these commands by simply deleting tu, nous, or vous from the indicative. Être gives sois, soyons, soyez; avoir gives aie, ayons, ayez. The forms resemble their present subjunctives, but a direct imperative has no que and no subject pronoun. Nous includes the speaker (let’s); vous addresses several people or one person politely.

The normal negative pattern still applies: ne sois pas, n’ayons pas, n’ayez pas. These forms work with the verb’s usual complement: être patient, avoir confiance, avoir peur. In sois patiente or soyez attentives, the adjective agrees with the people addressed, not with a written subject pronoun.
points: Être — be: sois (tu), soyons (nous), soyez (vous).
Avoir — have: aie (tu), ayons (nous), ayez (vous).

examples.french: Sois patient et aie confiance en tes progrès.
examples.english: Be patient and have confidence in your progress.
examples.note: Two singular familiar commands; addressing a woman, write patiente.

examples.french: Soyons attentifs et ayons du respect pour les opinions différentes.
examples.english: Let’s be attentive and show respect for differing opinions.
examples.note: The nous imperative includes the speaker; soyons and ayons are irregular.

examples.french: Soyez à l’heure et n’ayez pas peur de poser des questions.
examples.english: Be on time and do not be afraid to ask questions.
examples.note: Polite or plural vous; the negative surrounds ayez.

examples.french: N’aie pas honte de demander de l’aide.
examples.english: Do not be ashamed to ask for help.
examples.note: Aie has no final s, unlike the subjunctive form in que tu aies.

mistakes.avoid: Soiez attentifs pendant l’explication.
mistakes.prefer: Soyez attentifs pendant l’explication.
mistakes.why: The imperative vous form of être is soyez, with y.

mistakes.avoid: Aies confiance en tes progrès!
mistakes.prefer: Aie confiance en tes progrès!
mistakes.why: The tu imperative is aie; aies belongs to a subjunctive clause such as que tu aies.

vocabulary.example: Signez le formulaire au bas de la dernière page.
vocabulary.note: Regular `-er` verb; the `tu` imperative is `signe`, without `-s`.

vocabulary.example: Veuillez joindre une copie de votre pièce d’identité.
vocabulary.note: Formal imperative of `vouloir`, always followed by an infinitive.

vocabulary.example: Une vérification supplémentaire retarde parfois l’envoi du dossier.
vocabulary.note: Feminine noun; the ending -tion is a feminine hint.

vocabulary.example: Une copie numérisée est acceptée pour la première étape.
vocabulary.note: Feminine noun; `un exemplaire` refers to a printed copy of a document.

vocabulary.example: Agitez la bouteille avant de servir.
vocabulary.note: Regular `-er` verb; frequent on product labels in the imperative.

practice.prompt: Give the same instruction affirmatively and then negatively: send the file to them.
practice.hint: The pronoun order changes with the polarity.
practice.answer: Envoyez-le-leur. Ne le leur envoyez pas.

takeaways: Three persons only, no written subject.
`-er` verbs lose the `-s`, and recover it before `y` and `en`.
Affirmative equals pronouns after with hyphens; negative equals pronouns before.
Être: sois, soyons, soyez. Avoir: aie, ayons, ayez.
keywords: sois, soyons, soyez, aie, ayons, ayez

lessons.title: Le subjonctif présent et passé
lessons.summary: Choose the subjunctive after a trigger of will, emotion, doubt, necessity, judgement, concession, or purpose. The present can require two stems: que je prenne, but que nous prenions. The past combines a present-subjunctive auxiliary with a past participle: que j’aie terminé, qu’elle soit arrivée. It presents completion relative to a reference point, not necessarily an event before today. Learn the irregular forms and preserve ordinary auxiliary and agreement rules.
objectives: Recognise the trigger that requires a subjunctive.
Form one-stem and two-stem present subjunctives, including the nous/vous distinction.
Build the past subjunctive and explain completion or anteriority relative to a reference point.
Decide between an infinitive and a `que` clause.
Use `veiller à ce que`, `tenir à ce que`, and `s’attendre à ce que` with the full sequence.
Tell a decorative `ne` apart from a real negation in a subjunctive clause.

sections.title: Core concept
paragraphs: A mood is a set of verb forms expressing how an event is framed, rather than when it happens. The indicative commonly makes assertions; the subjunctive commonly occurs in a dependent clause, a group with its own subject and verb attached to another clause. Learn the construction that selects it: `il faut que`, `je veux que`, `je doute que`, `je suis content que`, `il est important que`, and conjunctions such as `pour que`, `afin que`, `bien que`, `avant que`, `à condition que`, `jusqu’à ce que`.

The subjunctive does not mean that an event is unreal or uncertain. `Je suis contente qu’elle soit ici` (I am glad she is here) can concern a known fact; the emotion construction selects the mood. Similarly, `bien que` concedes something despite which the main statement holds. Conversely, affirmative `espérer que` normally takes the indicative: `J’espère qu’elle viendra` (I hope she will come). Compare `Je pense qu’il est prêt` (I think he is ready) with `Je ne pense pas qu’il soit prêt` (I do not think he is ready): negating the opinion often favours the subjunctive, but mood still depends on how the speaker presents the information.

For many verbs, the present ils form minus -ent supplies the singular and third-person plural stem; nous and vous normally use the present nous stem minus -ons, with -ions and -iez. These stems coincide in réduire but differ in prendre: que je prenne, que nous prenions. Irregular verbs such as être and avoir need separate reference forms. With desire or purpose, an infinitive commonly keeps the same actor (Je veux partir; Je pars pour travailler); a que clause can name another actor (Je veux que tu partes). This is not a universal ban on same-subject subjunctive clauses. Après que takes the indicative in careful standard French.

Three useful constructions are `veiller à ce que` (to make sure that), `tenir à ce que` (to insist that), and `s’attendre à ce que` (to expect that), followed by the subjunctive: `Le service veille à ce que chaque demande soit traitée dans les délais`, `Nous tenons à ce que vous receviez une confirmation écrite`, `Je m’attends à ce qu’elle réponde avant vendredi`. Learn these full sequences. For `s’attendre`, the shorter `s’attendre que` plus subjunctive is also correct in a more formal register: `Je m’attends qu’elle réponde`.

After `avant que`, `à moins que`, `de peur que`, `de crainte que`, and `craindre que`, formal French may insert an optional, non-negative `ne`, called an expletive `ne`. `Je crains qu’elle ne soit déjà partie` means *I am afraid she has already left*. Do not identify this use merely by the absence of `pas`: a genuine negative can contain `jamais`, `plus`, `rien`, or `personne` instead. Compare `Je crains qu’elle ne soit pas informée` (*I am afraid she has not been informed*) and `Je crains qu’il ne revienne jamais` (*I am afraid he will never come back*). Read the whole clause and its meaning. Where `ne` is expletive, it can be omitted without changing the meaning: `avant que le délai expire` and `avant que le délai n’expire`.
points: Look for the trigger in the main clause before choosing the mood.
Check both the present ils stem and the nous stem before forming the subjunctive.
Learn irregular paradigms rather than treating the ordinary ending rule as universal.
Prefer an infinitive for the same actor with constructions such as vouloir and pour.
Keep the indicative after `après que`.
Add `souhaiter que` and `vouloir que` to the list of will triggers.
Learn veiller à ce que, tenir à ce que, and the common s’attendre à ce que; formal s’attendre que is also accepted.
Recognise the optional expletive `ne` after triggers such as `avant que` and `craindre que`.
Check the whole clause for real negation: `ne… pas`, `ne… jamais`, `ne… plus`, and other negative expressions.

examples.french: Il faut que nous réduisions la pollution dans les centres urbains.
examples.english: We must reduce pollution in urban centres.
examples.note: Regular formation from « ils réduisent ».

examples.french: Je suis heureuse que ma candidature ait été retenue.
examples.english: I am glad that my application was accepted.
examples.note: Past subjunctive in a passive construction: ait été retenue describes an acceptance completed before the present happiness.

examples.french: Je vous écris pour que vous connaissiez ma situation actuelle.
examples.english: I am writing so that you are aware of my current situation.
examples.note: Purpose with two different subjects.

examples.french: Je vous écris pour expliquer ma situation actuelle.
examples.english: I am writing to explain my current situation.
examples.note: Same subject, so an infinitive replaces the que clause.

examples.french: Bien que le dossier soit complet, il faut encore attendre la décision.
examples.english: Although the file is complete, we still have to wait for the decision.
examples.note: Bien que normally selects the subjunctive in a concessive clause, even when the file really is complete.

examples.french: Le service veille à ce que chaque demande soit traitée dans les délais annoncés.
examples.english: The department makes sure that every application is processed within the announced deadlines.
examples.note: « Veiller » keeps the full sequence « à ce que » before the subjunctive.

examples.french: Nous tenons à ce que vous receviez une confirmation écrite, et je m’attends à ce qu’elle parte lundi.
examples.english: We insist that you receive a written confirmation, and I expect it to be sent on Monday.
examples.note: « Tenir à ce que » and « s’attendre à ce que » follow the same pattern.

examples.french: Je crains qu’elle ne soit déjà partie, mais je crains surtout qu’elle ne soit pas informée.
examples.english: I am afraid she has already left, but above all I am afraid she has not been informed.
examples.note: The first « ne » is decorative; the second is a real negation because « pas » is present.

examples.french: Nous partirons à moins qu’il ne pleuve, et déposez votre demande avant que le délai n’expire.
examples.english: We will leave unless it rains, and submit your application before the deadline expires.
examples.note: The optional « ne » adds a formal tone without changing the meaning.

examples.french: Je crains qu’il ne revienne jamais au bureau.
examples.english: I am afraid he will never come back to the office.
examples.note: « Ne… jamais » is a real negation even though there is no pas.

mistakes.avoid: Après qu’il soit parti, nous avons commencé la réunion.
mistakes.prefer: Après qu’il est parti, nous avons commencé la réunion.
mistakes.why: In careful standard French, `après que` introduces a fact and takes the indicative.

mistakes.avoid: Je veux que tu pars plus tôt aujourd’hui.
mistakes.prefer: Je veux que tu partes plus tôt aujourd’hui.
mistakes.why: Vouloir que selects the subjunctive partes, not indicative pars.

mistakes.avoid: Le responsable veille que tout soit prêt avant l’ouverture.
mistakes.prefer: Le responsable veille à ce que tout soit prêt avant l’ouverture.
mistakes.why: `Veiller` governs `à ce que` before a clause; the sequence cannot be shortened to `que`.

mistakes.avoid: Nous veillons à ce que le dossier est complet avant l’envoi.
mistakes.prefer: Nous veillons à ce que le dossier soit complet avant l’envoi.
mistakes.why: Veiller à ce que selects the subjunctive soit. The choice follows this construction, not a claim that the file cannot in fact be complete.

mistakes.avoid: Déposez votre demande avant qu’il ne vient au guichet.
mistakes.prefer: Déposez votre demande avant qu’il ne vienne au guichet.
mistakes.why: The optional `ne` does not change the mood: `avant que` still requires the subjunctive.

sections.title: Present subjunctive: two stems and irregular reference forms
paragraphs: The ordinary endings are -e, -es, -e, -ions, -iez, -ent. For prendre, ils prennent gives prenn- for je, tu, il/elle/on, and ils/elles; nous prenons gives pren- for nous and vous. Thus prenne/prennes/prenne/prenions/preniez/prennent is one paradigm, not six applications of prenn-. Vouloir uses veuill- in the singular and third-person plural, but voul- for nous/vous. Aller similarly contrasts aill- with all-.

The following full reference lines use the order je, tu, il/elle/on, nous, vous, ils/elles; place que or qu’ before the subject in a clause. Être and avoir are especially important because their subjunctives also form compound tenses.
points: Prendre — to take: prenne, prennes, prenne, prenions, preniez, prennent.
Vouloir — to want: veuille, veuilles, veuille, voulions, vouliez, veuillent.
Aller — to go: aille, ailles, aille, allions, alliez, aillent.
Être — to be: sois, sois, soit, soyons, soyez, soient.
Avoir — to have: aie, aies, ait, ayons, ayez, aient.
Faire — to do/make: fasse, fasses, fasse, fassions, fassiez, fassent.
Pouvoir — to be able to: puisse, puisses, puisse, puissions, puissiez, puissent.
Savoir — to know: sache, saches, sache, sachions, sachiez, sachent.

examples.french: Il faut qu’elle prenne le train et que nous prenions l’autobus.
examples.english: She needs to take the train, and we need to take the bus.
examples.note: Prenne uses prenn-; prenions uses pren-.

examples.french: Je comprends qu’ils veuillent une réponse et que vous vouliez vérifier les chiffres.
examples.english: I understand their wanting an answer and your wanting to check the figures.
examples.note: Comprendre here expresses understanding of a wish; contrast veuillent with vouliez.

examples.french: Il est préférable qu’il aille au bureau et que vous alliez à la réunion.
examples.english: It is preferable for him to go to the office and for you to go to the meeting.
examples.note: Aller also has separate aill- and all- stems.

examples.french: Il faut que nous soyons prêts et que vous ayez une pièce d’identité.
examples.english: We must be ready, and you must have identification.
