`le salé (m.)` — savoury foods as a category; the adjective `salé / salée` can mean salty or salted.
`la mousse (f.)` — foam, froth, lather; `la mousse de lait (f.)` — milk foam.
Use context for this noun: `la mousse au chocolat (f.)` is a dessert, whereas `la mousse du savon (f.)` is soap lather.

examples.french: Pour le buffet du bureau, prévoyons du sucré et du salé : des gâteaux et des tartes aux légumes.
examples.english: For the office buffet, let's provide sweet and savoury food: cakes and vegetable tarts.
examples.note: The two category nouns organise the menu.

examples.french: Je préfère le salé au sucré, mais cette soupe est trop salée à mon goût.
examples.english: I prefer savoury food to sweet food, but this soup is too salty for my taste.
examples.note: Savoury as a category is different from too salty as a flavour judgement.

examples.french: Cette sauce a un goût de citron ; elle accompagne bien les légumes.
examples.english: This sauce tastes of lemon; it goes well with the vegetables.
examples.note: Un goût de names the identifiable flavour.

examples.french: La mousse de lait forme une couche de petites bulles sur le café.
examples.english: The milk foam forms a layer of tiny bubbles on the coffee.
examples.note: This explicitly describes physical foam.

examples.french: Rincez les assiettes jusqu’à ce qu’il ne reste plus de mousse.
examples.english: Rinse the plates until no lather remains.
examples.note: In dishwashing, mousse is soap lather, not a dessert.

examples.french: La mousse au chocolat a un goût intense, mais elle n’est pas très sucrée.
examples.english: The chocolate mousse has an intense flavour, but it is not very sweet.
examples.note: Here mousse names an airy dessert; sucrée describes its sweetness.

mistakes.avoid: Cette soupe est trop salé.
mistakes.prefer: Cette soupe est trop salée.
mistakes.why: Salée agrees with feminine soupe. Trop salée means too salty; le salé as a food category means savoury food, not excessive salt.

mistakes.avoid: Il reste du mousse de lait sur le café.
mistakes.prefer: Il reste de la mousse de lait sur le café.
mistakes.why: Mousse is feminine, including when it means foam.

sections.title: Cooking from a recipe and baking biscuits
paragraphs: `Cuisiner` means to cook or prepare food, either as an activity or with a direct object. It is distinct from `la cuisine (f.)`, which can mean the kitchen or cooking as a noun. `Une recette (f.)` gives the ingredients and method; `un livre de cuisine (m.)` is a cookbook containing recipes.
`Faire des biscuits` means to make or bake biscuits or cookies. The phrase can include mixing and shaping as well as baking. `Faire cuire les biscuits` focuses specifically on cooking them with heat.
points: `cuisiner` — cook, prepare food: `J’aime cuisiner`, `Je cuisine des légumes`.
`une recette (f.)` — recipe; `suivre une recette` — follow a recipe.
`un livre de cuisine (m.)` — cookbook; it contains more than one recipe.
`le poivre (m.)` — pepper used as a seasoning, not the vegetable `un poivron (m.)`, a bell pepper.
`un biscuit (m.)`, `des biscuits (m. pl.)` — biscuit or cookie, biscuits or cookies; `faire des biscuits` — make or bake biscuits.

examples.french: Je cuisine le dimanche pour préparer les repas que j’emporte au travail.
examples.english: I cook on Sundays to prepare the meals I take to work.
examples.note: Cuisiner names the activity of preparing food.

examples.french: Cette recette vient d’un livre de cuisine emprunté à la bibliothèque.
examples.english: This recipe comes from a cookbook borrowed from the library.
examples.note: The recipe is one set of instructions; the cookbook is the whole publication.

examples.french: La recette demande du poivre, mais pas de poivron.
examples.english: The recipe calls for pepper seasoning, but no bell pepper.
examples.note: The two similar-looking words name different ingredients.

examples.french: Nous allons faire des biscuits pour la réunion des voisins ; j’ai déjà sorti le beurre.
examples.english: We are going to bake biscuits for the neighbours' meeting; I have already taken out the butter.
examples.note: Faire des biscuits covers preparing and baking them.

examples.french: J’ai suivi la recette du livre de cuisine, puis j’ai fait cuire les biscuits pendant douze minutes.
examples.english: I followed the recipe in the cookbook, then baked the biscuits for twelve minutes.
examples.note: Faire cuire identifies the heating stage and its duration.

mistakes.avoid: J’aime cuisine après le travail.
mistakes.prefer: J’aime cuisiner après le travail.
mistakes.why: To say you like doing the activity, use the infinitive cuisiner. La cuisine is the corresponding noun.

mistakes.avoid: Ajoutez du poivron moulu.
mistakes.prefer: Ajoutez du poivre moulu.
mistakes.why: If the intended seasoning is black pepper, use le poivre. The first phrase can describe ground bell pepper, but it names a different ingredient.

vocabulary.example: Le pain frais est distribué chaque matin à la banque alimentaire.
vocabulary.note: Masculine noun; `du pain` for an unspecified amount.

vocabulary.example: La confiture de fraises est préparée avec les fruits du jardin.
vocabulary.note: Feminine noun; `de la confiture` for an unspecified amount.

vocabulary.example: Les céréales complètes apportent davantage de fibres au petit déjeuner.
vocabulary.note: Feminine plural noun; normally used in the plural in this sense.

vocabulary.example: La moitié des participants a choisi la visite guidée.
vocabulary.note: Feminine noun; `la moitié de` plus a determined noun.

vocabulary.example: Une banque alimentaire soutient les familles à faible revenu du quartier.
vocabulary.note: Feminine noun phrase; the gender comes from `banque`.

vocabulary.example: Le déjeuner est servi de sept heures à neuf heures.
vocabulary.note: Masculine noun; the meal it names depends on the region.

vocabulary.example: Le souper communautaire réunit les voisins le premier vendredi du mois.
vocabulary.note: Masculine noun used in Canada; `le dîner` names the evening meal in France.

vocabulary.example: Le raisin local arrive sur les marchés à la fin de l’été.
vocabulary.note: Masculine noun, usually singular for the fruit as a food: `du raisin`.

vocabulary.example: Le restaurant propose un menu végétarien et une option végétalienne.
vocabulary.note: Doubles the `n` in the feminine, like `canadien / canadienne`.

practice.prompt: Complete: « Je voudrais ___ eau, un litre ___ lait et ___ pommes ; il n’y a plus ___ sucre. »
practice.hint: Partitive, quantity, partitive, negation.
practice.answer: Je voudrais de l’eau, un litre de lait et des pommes ; il n’y a plus de sucre.

takeaways: Unmeasured food takes `du`, `de la`, `de l’`, `des`.
General quantities and denied amounts normally use de; portions of a known whole can retain its definite article.
A rate uses the definite article: `trois dollars le kilo`.
keywords: demi- devant un nom, une demi-bouteille, la moitié de
végétarien, végétarienne, une assiette, le beurre, le raisin
le goût, le sucré, le salé, la mousse
cuisiner, une recette, le poivre, un livre de cuisine, faire des biscuits

lessons.title: La maison, les voyages et les services
lessons.summary: Everyday service situations rely on fixed phrases that are faster to reuse than to build word by word: `Où se trouve…, s’il vous plaît ?`, `au rez-de-chaussée`, `au premier étage`, `au fond du couloir`, `réserver une voiture de location`, `faire les courses`. Note that `faire les courses` means grocery shopping, while leisure shopping is `faire du shopping` or `faire les magasins`.
objectives: Ask where a service is located in a polite, ready-made form.
Understand floor and direction indications.
Separate grocery shopping from leisure shopping.

sections.title: Core concept
paragraphs: A lexical chunk is a multiword expression learned as a unit, then adapted to the situation. It can make common service requests easier to produce: Pardon, où se trouve le bureau d’accueil, s’il vous plaît ? Change the noun and, when necessary, the verb: Où se trouvent les toilettes ? You can also build a different question: Où est-ce que je peux payer ?

In the usual French convention, le rez-de-chaussée is the ground level and le premier étage is the level above it. British English generally follows this distinction; North American English often calls the ground level the first floor. Do not assume that English first floor always differs from premier étage. Check a building’s signs or ask if its numbering is unclear. Useful directions include au fond du couloir, en face de l’ascenseur, à droite and à gauche.

Faire les courses usually means buying groceries or everyday necessities. Faire du shopping and faire les magasins often involve visiting shops or browsing, but they are not restricted to unnecessary purchases; meanings can overlap. Devoir also needs context, not just number: un devoir can be an obligation or a school assignment; les devoirs can be homework or duties.
points: Open a request with `Pardon` and close it with `s’il vous plaît`.
Use `Où se trouve` plus a singular noun and `Où se trouvent` plus a plural.
Read `le rez-de-chaussée` as the ground floor and `le premier étage` as the one above.
Reuse the direction chunks: `au fond de`, `en face de`, `à droite`, `à gauche`.
Use `faire les courses` for groceries and `faire du shopping` for leisure.
Use `retirer` for taking money out and `déposer` for paying it in.
Use context to distinguish un devoir or des devoirs as obligations from schoolwork.

examples.french: Pardon, où se trouve le bureau d’accueil, s’il vous plaît ?
examples.english: Excuse me, where is the reception desk, please?
examples.note: The standard polite request frame.

examples.french: Le bureau d’accueil est au rez-de-chaussée de l’hôtel de ville.
examples.english: The reception desk is on the ground floor of city hall.
examples.note: Rez-de-chaussée names the ground level; in North American English this may also be called the first floor.

examples.french: Le service des permis est au premier étage, au fond du couloir.
examples.english: The permits office is one floor up, at the end of the corridor.
examples.note: Two chunks combined in a direction.

examples.french: Nous devons réserver une voiture de location pour visiter la région.
examples.english: We need to book a rental car to visit the region.
examples.note: Fixed expression for renting a vehicle.

examples.french: Nous finissons notre dîner avant d’aller faire les courses.
examples.english: We finish lunch before going grocery shopping.
examples.note: In Canada « le dîner » is the midday meal; « faire les courses » is grocery shopping.

examples.french: Je dois retirer de l’argent à la banque avant de rentrer.
examples.english: I need to withdraw some money at the bank before going home.
examples.note: « Retirer de l’argent » is the standard expression; « déposer » is its opposite.

examples.french: Pour moi, aider les autres est un devoir ; ce soir, j’aide ma fille à faire ses devoirs.
examples.english: For me, helping others is a duty; tonight, I am helping my daughter with her homework.
examples.note: The context distinguishes an obligation from schoolwork. Un devoir de mathématiques can also name one assignment.

mistakes.avoid: Pardon, où se trouvent le bureau d’accueil, s’il vous plaît ?
mistakes.prefer: Pardon, où se trouve le bureau d’accueil, s’il vous plaît ?
mistakes.why: `Se trouver` agrees with its subject; `le bureau d’accueil` is singular, so the verb stays singular.

mistakes.avoid: Je vais faire du shopping : il me faut du lait et du pain.
mistakes.prefer: Je vais faire les courses : il me faut du lait et du pain.
mistakes.why: Both sentences are grammatical. Faire les courses is the usual expression for grocery shopping; faire du shopping more often suggests visiting shops or browsing.

mistakes.avoid: Mon fils termine son devoir de mathématiques et ses autres devoir ce soir.
mistakes.prefer: Mon fils termine son devoir de mathématiques et ses autres devoirs ce soir.
mistakes.why: A single assignment is `un devoir`, and the plural `des devoirs` covers the whole set of schoolwork.

sections.title: Furnishing a living room and finding storage
paragraphs: In a housing description, `le salon (m.)` is the living room. `Un canapé (m.)` and `un sofa (m.)` both mean a sofa or couch; they do not name different types of furniture. `Canapé` is the usual everyday choice in France, while the frequency of `sofa` varies by region.

`Installer les meubles` means putting the furniture in place, not necessarily assembling it. A listing that mentions `un placard (m.)` promises storage, not another bedroom: depending on the setting, it is a cupboard or a closet.
points: `le salon (m.)` — living room, in a home.
`un canapé (m.)`, `un sofa (m.)` — sofa, couch.
`un placard (m.)` — cupboard or closet; specify what it holds when the English translation depends on context.
`un miroir (m.)` — mirror, not a window.
`un meuble (m.)`, `les meubles (m. pl.)` — a piece of furniture, furniture; `installer les meubles` — put the furniture in place.

examples.french: Le salon est assez grand pour un canapé et une petite table.
examples.english: The living room is large enough for a sofa and a small table.
examples.note: A useful way to describe the space during an apartment viewing.

examples.french: L’annonce mentionne un sofa : est-ce le canapé que l’on voit sur la photo ?
examples.english: The listing mentions a sofa: is it the couch shown in the photo?
examples.note: The two furniture words refer to the same kind of seat.

examples.french: Dans l’entrée, le miroir est fixé à la porte du placard.
examples.english: In the entrance hall, the mirror is attached to the closet door.
examples.note: The location makes the closet meaning natural.

examples.french: Nous allons installer les meubles dans le salon avant de ranger les cartons.
examples.english: We are going to put the furniture in place in the living room before putting the boxes away.
examples.note: This describes arranging the room, not constructing the furniture.

examples.french: Il y a un placard pour la vaisselle, mais aucun placard pour les vêtements.
examples.english: There is a cupboard for the dishes, but no closet for clothes.
examples.note: The same French noun covers two kinds of storage.

mistakes.avoid: Nous avons installé deux furnitures dans le salon.
mistakes.prefer: Nous avons installé deux meubles dans le salon.
mistakes.why: French uses the countable noun `un meuble (m.)`; English furniture is not a French noun.

mistakes.avoid: Le canapé est dans la salon.
mistakes.prefer: Le canapé est dans le salon.
mistakes.why: The living-room noun `le salon (m.)` is masculine.

sections.title: Describing decoration and requesting repairs
paragraphs: Separate the surface, its covering, and the tool used on it. `Un plafond (m.)` is the ceiling; `le papier peint (m.)` is wallpaper, not wet paint. `Un pinceau (m.)` is a paintbrush. These distinctions help a landlord or a repair service understand what needs attention.
`La douche (f.)` can name the shower installation or the act of showering. `La douche fuit` reports a leaking fixture; `prendre une douche` means to have a shower.
points: `un plafond (m.)` — ceiling; the spelling is `plafond`, without a t.
`le papier peint (m.)` — wallpaper; `la peinture (f.)` — paint, the material applied with a brush.
`un pinceau (m.)`, `des pinceaux (m. pl.)` — paintbrush, paintbrushes.
`un rideau (m.)`, `des rideaux (m. pl.)` — curtain, curtains.
`la douche (f.)` — shower; `prendre une douche` — have a shower.

examples.french: Le papier peint se décolle près de la fenêtre, mais le plafond est en bon état.
examples.english: The wallpaper is peeling near the window, but the ceiling is in good condition.
examples.note: Two separate parts of the room are described in a maintenance report.

examples.french: J’ai utilisé un petit pinceau pour peindre le bord du plafond.
examples.english: I used a small paintbrush to paint the edge of the ceiling.
examples.note: The brush is the tool; the ceiling is the surface.

examples.french: Faut-il enlever les rideaux avant de remplacer le papier peint ?
examples.english: Should we take down the curtains before replacing the wallpaper?
examples.note: A practical question before decorating.

examples.french: La douche fuit et une tache apparaît au plafond de l’appartement du dessous.
examples.english: The shower is leaking, and a stain is appearing on the ceiling of the apartment below.
examples.note: Here the shower is the installation, not the act of washing.

examples.french: Après avoir nettoyé les pinceaux, je vais prendre une douche.
examples.english: After cleaning the paintbrushes, I am going to have a shower.
examples.note: The plural is pinceaux; prendre une douche names the activity.

mistakes.avoid: Le platfond doit être réparé.
mistakes.prefer: Le plafond doit être réparé.
mistakes.why: The noun for ceiling is spelled `plafond`, not `platfond`.

mistakes.avoid: Nous avons lavé les pinceaus et les rideaus.
mistakes.prefer: Nous avons lavé les pinceaux et les rideaux.
mistakes.why: These two nouns form their plurals in -eaux.

sections.title: Checking appliances, screens, and internet access
paragraphs: When checking what a rental or shared workspace provides, distinguish the devices by their purpose: `une cafetière (f.)` makes coffee; `une bouilloire (f.)` heats water. `Un écran (m.)` displays images, whereas `une caméra (f.)` records video. A camera for still photographs is normally `un appareil photo (m.)`.

`La télévision (f.)` can mean television as a medium or a television set in everyday speech. For internet access, learn the request `Quel est le mot de passe du wifi ?` as a practical service question.
points: `une cafetière (f.)` — coffee maker; `une bouilloire (f.)` — kettle.
`la télévision (f.)` — television; `regarder la télévision` — watch television.
`une caméra (f.)` — video camera, including a surveillance camera.
`un écran (m.)` — screen, whether on a computer, television, or information display.
`le wifi (m.)` — Wi-Fi; `Il y a du wifi` — Wi-Fi is available.
`un mot de passe (m.)` — password; `le mot de passe du wifi` — the Wi-Fi password.

examples.french: La cuisine commune dispose d’une cafetière et d’une bouilloire.
examples.english: The shared kitchen has a coffee maker and a kettle.
examples.note: Two appliances with different functions.

examples.french: La bouilloire fonctionne, mais la cafetière ne chauffe plus.
examples.english: The kettle works, but the coffee maker no longer heats up.
examples.note: Name the faulty appliance when reporting a problem.

examples.french: La télévision du salon a un grand écran, mais il n’y a pas de wifi dans la chambre.
examples.english: The living-room television has a large screen, but there is no Wi-Fi in the bedroom.
examples.note: A television set, its screen, and internet access are distinct amenities.

examples.french: Une caméra de surveillance filme l’entrée ; les images apparaissent sur l’écran de la réception.
examples.english: A surveillance camera films the entrance; the images appear on the screen at reception.
examples.note: The camera captures the images; the screen displays them.

examples.french: Il y a du wifi dans cette salle ? J’ai un entretien en ligne à quinze heures.
examples.english: Is there Wi-Fi in this room? I have an online interview at three p.m.
examples.note: A natural spoken question about access before a work appointment.

examples.french: Le mot de passe du wifi a changé ; pourriez-vous me donner le nouveau ?
examples.english: The Wi-Fi password has changed; could you give me the new one?
examples.note: Ask for the password without confusing it with the network name.

mistakes.avoid: Quelle est la mot de passe du wifi ?
mistakes.prefer: Quel est le mot de passe du wifi ?
mistakes.why: `Un mot de passe (m.)` is masculine, so both the question word and the article are masculine.

mistakes.avoid: Nous avons acheté un caméra de surveillance.
mistakes.prefer: Nous avons acheté une caméra de surveillance.
mistakes.why: Caméra is feminine. Une caméra is the usual name for a video device; un appareil photo names a still camera, even though modern devices may do both.

sections.title: Appointments, shopping centres, and change
paragraphs: `Un agenda (m.)` is a diary or planner for appointments, on paper or online. It is not necessarily a personal journal; that is `un journal intime (m.)`. The list of topics for a meeting is `un ordre du jour (m.)`.

For payment, `la monnaie (f.)` can mean coins or the change returned after paying. `Une bourse (f.)` can be a small pouch for coins, often with a drawstring; it is not a universal translation of wallet. The phrase `pour toutes les bourses` uses the same noun figuratively to mean for every budget.
points: `un agenda (m.)` — appointment diary, planner.
`un centre commercial (m.)` — shopping centre, mall.
`la monnaie (f.)` — change: coins or money returned after a payment; `rendre la monnaie` — give change.
`une bourse (f.)` — small coin pouch; in `pour toutes les bourses`, a person's financial means or budget.
`un portefeuille (m.)` — wallet for notes and cards; `un porte-monnaie (m.)` — coin purse, the more usual everyday word when asking for an item to hold coins.

examples.french: J’ai noté dans mon agenda le rendez-vous à la banque du centre commercial.
examples.english: I wrote the appointment at the bank in the shopping centre in my planner.
examples.note: The planner records when and where the appointment takes place.

examples.french: Au centre commercial, le distributeur de boissons n’accepte que la monnaie.
examples.english: At the shopping centre, the drinks machine only accepts coins.
examples.note: Here change means coins, not money in general.

examples.french: J’ai payé avec vingt euros, et la caissière m’a rendu cinq euros de monnaie.
examples.english: I paid with twenty euros, and the cashier gave me five euros in change.
examples.note: Change returned after a payment may include notes as well as coins.

examples.french: Elle garde quelques pièces dans une petite bourse en tissu et ses cartes dans son portefeuille.
examples.english: She keeps a few coins in a small cloth pouch and her cards in her wallet.
examples.note: The pouch and the wallet are different objects.

examples.french: Ce centre commercial propose des restaurants pour toutes les bourses.
examples.english: This shopping centre offers restaurants for every budget.
examples.note: The plural expression concerns affordability, not the design of coin pouches.

mistakes.avoid: Je note mes rendez-vous de la semaine dans mon ordre du jour.
mistakes.prefer: Je note mes rendez-vous de la semaine dans mon agenda.
mistakes.why: An appointment planner is un agenda (m.); un ordre du jour (m.) lists the topics for a particular meeting.

mistakes.avoid: Il y a des restaurants pour tous les bourses.
mistakes.prefer: Il y a des restaurants pour toutes les bourses.
mistakes.why: Bourse is feminine, so use toutes. The expression means for every budget, not literally for all coin purses.

sections.title: Leaving on holiday: platforms, luggage, and camping
paragraphs: `Partir en vacances` means to go away on holiday. At a station, `un quai (m.)` is the platform where passengers wait; `une voie (f.)` is the track. An information display may give the track number even though you stand on the platform.

At a station or hotel, `la consigne (f.)` can be a luggage-storage service or facility. This is a different meaning from `une consigne (f.)`, an instruction. `Un bagage (m.)` is one piece of luggage; French can count it directly.

`Le camping (m.)` names camping as an activity, while `un camping (m.)` is a campsite or campground. The surrounding phrase makes the meaning clear: `faire du camping` but `réserver une place dans un camping`.
points: `partir en vacances` — go away on holiday; `les vacances (f. pl.)` is plural in this expression.
`un quai (m.)` — train platform; `un rang (m.)` — row, as in a row of seats, not a station platform.
`la consigne (f.)` — luggage storage in a travel-service context; `laisser ses bagages à la consigne` — leave one's luggage in storage.
`un bagage (m.)`, `des bagages (m. pl.)` — a piece of luggage, luggage.
`une tente (f.)` — tent; `monter une tente` — put up a tent.
`le camping (m.)` — camping; `un camping (m.)` — campsite or campground.

examples.french: Nous partons en vacances vendredi et nous emportons deux bagages.
examples.english: We are going away on holiday on Friday and taking two pieces of luggage.
examples.note: French counts individual bags with the plural bagages.

examples.french: Avant de rejoindre le quai, j’ai laissé mon gros bagage à la consigne.
examples.english: Before going to the platform, I left my large piece of luggage in storage.
examples.note: The service stores a physical bag; no instructions are meant here.

examples.french: L’écran indique la voie 4 ; les voyageurs attendent sur le quai.
examples.english: The screen shows track 4; the passengers are waiting on the platform.
examples.note: The track and the place where passengers stand are not the same thing.

examples.french: À l’hôtel, la consigne est gratuite, mais il faut récupérer les bagages avant dix-huit heures.
examples.english: At the hotel, luggage storage is free, but you must collect your luggage before six p.m.
examples.note: A realistic service condition.

examples.french: Nous avons réservé une place dans un camping où nous pourrons monter notre tente.
examples.english: We have booked a pitch at a campsite where we can put up our tent.
examples.note: The countable noun identifies an accommodation site.

examples.french: Je préfère faire du camping plutôt que dormir à l’hôtel pendant les vacances.
examples.english: I prefer camping to sleeping in a hotel during the holidays.
examples.note: Here camping is the activity, not a particular site.

examples.french: Dans l’autocar, nos places sont au deuxième rang, juste derrière le conducteur.
examples.english: On the coach, our seats are in the second row, just behind the driver.
examples.note: A row of seats is un rang (m.); a railway platform is un quai (m.).

mistakes.avoid: Nous partons en vacance demain.
mistakes.prefer: Nous partons en vacances demain.
mistakes.why: The holiday expression uses the plural vacances.

mistakes.avoid: Allez au consigne pour y déposer votre valise.
mistakes.prefer: Allez à la consigne pour y déposer votre valise.
mistakes.why: Consigne is feminine, so use à la. Here it means luggage storage; lire une consigne would mean read an instruction.

sections.title: Birthdays, toys, and dressing up
paragraphs: `Un anniversaire (m.)` is a birthday when it concerns a person's birth. The same noun also means an anniversary: `un anniversaire de mariage (m.)` is a wedding anniversary. The extra words or the situation establish which event you mean.

For a children's party or a dress-up box, distinguish `un jouet (m.)`, a toy, from items worn on the head: `un chapeau (m.)` is a hat, while `une couronne (f.)` is a crown. A paper crown can be a costume accessory without being an ordinary hat.
points: `un anniversaire (m.)` — birthday; anniversary of an event.
`un jouet (m.)`, `des jouets (m. pl.)` — toy, toys.
`un chapeau (m.)`, `des chapeaux (m. pl.)` — hat, hats.
`une couronne (f.)` — crown; `une couronne en papier (f.)` — paper crown.

examples.french: Pour l’anniversaire de ma fille, nous avons fabriqué des couronnes en papier.
examples.english: For my daughter's birthday, we made paper crowns.
examples.note: The family context identifies a birthday, not another anniversary.

examples.french: Les enfants ont rangé les jouets avant de décorer le salon pour l’anniversaire.
examples.english: The children put the toys away before decorating the living room for the birthday.
examples.note: The plural toys are ordinary countable objects.

examples.french: Dans la boîte à déguisements, il y a deux chapeaux et une couronne.
examples.english: In the dress-up box, there are two hats and a crown.
examples.note: The crown is a separate kind of headwear; the plural of chapeau ends in -x.

examples.french: Ce jouet est destiné aux enfants de plus de trois ans ; vérifions avant de l’offrir pour son anniversaire.
examples.english: This toy is intended for children over three; let's check before giving it to him for his birthday.
examples.note: A practical shopping context for a toy.

examples.french: Ce n’est pas son anniversaire aujourd’hui : nous fêtons leur anniversaire de mariage.
examples.english: It is not her birthday today: we are celebrating their wedding anniversary.
examples.note: The same noun has two event-related meanings.

mistakes.avoid: Nous préparons une anniversaire avec deux chapeaus en papier.
mistakes.prefer: Nous préparons un anniversaire avec deux chapeaux en papier.
mistakes.why: Anniversaire is masculine, and chapeau has the plural chapeaux.

sections.title: Pets and the behaviour you notice at home
paragraphs: `Un animal familier (m.)` is an animal kept as a companion; the more usual everyday expression is `un animal de compagnie (m.)`. Do not assume every animal seen near a home is a pet: `une souris (f.)` can be a pet mouse or a wild one.

`Miauler` is the sound a cat makes: to meow. `Se gratter` means to scratch oneself, and `agiter la queue` means to wag or move the tail. Tail movement alone does not tell you that an animal is friendly.
points: `un animal familier (m.)`, `un animal de compagnie (m.)` — pet; plural `des animaux familiers (m. pl.)`, `des animaux de compagnie (m. pl.)`.
`une souris (f.)` — mouse; its singular and plural spellings are the same. Here it is the animal, not the computer device or the verb in `je souris`.
`miauler` — meow: `le chat miaule`, the cat meows.
`se gratter` — scratch oneself, for a person or an animal.
`la queue (f.)` — tail in this animal context; `agiter la queue` — wag or move the tail.

examples.french: Le bail autorise un animal de compagnie ; ma fille aimerait avoir une souris.
examples.english: The lease allows one pet; my daughter would like to have a mouse.
examples.note: The mouse is a proposed household pet.

examples.french: Le formulaire demande si nous avons des animaux familiers ; nous avons indiqué notre chat.
examples.english: The form asks whether we have pets; we listed our cat.
examples.note: Animaux familiers is understood as pets, though animaux de compagnie is more usual.

examples.french: Le chat miaule devant la porte, tandis que le chien agite la queue à notre arrivée.
examples.english: The cat meows at the door, while the dog wags its tail when we arrive.
examples.note: One verb names a sound; the other phrase describes a movement.

examples.french: Notre chien se gratte souvent derrière l’oreille ; nous avons pris rendez-vous chez le vétérinaire.
examples.english: Our dog often scratches behind its ear; we have made an appointment with the vet.
examples.note: Se gratter means the dog is scratching itself, not another animal.

examples.french: Une souris est entrée dans le placard, et le chat s’est mis à miauler.
examples.english: A mouse went into the cupboard, and the cat started meowing.
examples.note: The mouse is not presented as a pet in this household incident.

mistakes.avoid: Mon chien gratte souvent, même quand il est seul.
mistakes.prefer: Mon chien se gratte souvent, même quand il est seul.
mistakes.why: If the dog scratches itself, keep se. Without it, gratter may describe scratching the floor, a door, or something else.

mistakes.avoid: Une sourie se cache dans le placard.
mistakes.prefer: Une souris se cache dans le placard.
mistakes.why: The animal noun ends in -s even in the singular.

vocabulary.example: Le bureau d’accueil fournit un plan aux nouveaux visiteurs.
vocabulary.note: Masculine compound; `l’accueil` alone also means reception.

vocabulary.example: Le rez-de-chaussée abrite la réception et la salle d’attente.
vocabulary.note: Masculine noun; invariable in the plural.

vocabulary.example: Une voiture de location nous permettra d’explorer la région.
vocabulary.note: Feminine noun phrase; the gender comes from `voiture`.

vocabulary.example: Nous faisons les courses le samedi matin au marché du quartier.
vocabulary.note: Distinct from `faire du shopping`, which is leisure shopping.

vocabulary.example: Un arrêt d’autobus se trouve juste devant l’immeuble.
vocabulary.note: Masculine compound; `un arrêt de bus` is the usual form in France.

vocabulary.example: Elle a retiré cent dollars au guichet automatique.
vocabulary.note: Regular `-er` verb; `retirer une candidature` also means to withdraw an application.

vocabulary.example: Un ordinateur public est disponible à la bibliothèque du quartier.
vocabulary.note: Masculine noun; `un ordinateur portable` is a laptop.

vocabulary.example: La télévision de la salle d’attente diffuse les consignes en boucle.
vocabulary.note: Feminine noun; the clipped form `la télé` is informal.

vocabulary.example: Un canapé confortable occupe le fond du salon.
vocabulary.note: Masculine noun; `un sofa` is a common synonym.

vocabulary.example: Un verre d’eau est offert à chaque visiteur.
vocabulary.note: Masculine noun; also names the material glass.

vocabulary.example: Un outil en ligne permet de calculer les frais de dossier.
vocabulary.note: Masculine noun; the final `l` is silent.

vocabulary.example: Une caméra de surveillance filme l’entrée du bâtiment.
vocabulary.note: Feminine noun for a video camera; a photo camera is `un appareil photo`.

vocabulary.example: Le devoir de réserve s’applique à tous les employés du service.
vocabulary.note: Les devoirs can mean homework or obligations; un devoir can also be a single school assignment. Context selects the meaning.

vocabulary.example: La caissière m’a rendu la monnaie sur vingt dollars.
vocabulary.note: Feminine noun; `l’argent` is money in general.

vocabulary.example: Un agenda partagé évite les rendez-vous en double.
vocabulary.note: Masculine noun despite its final -a.

vocabulary.example: Une cafetière est à la disposition du personnel dans la cuisine.
vocabulary.note: Feminine noun; `une bouilloire` boils water for tea.

vocabulary.example: Une bouilloire électrique chauffe l’eau en deux minutes.
vocabulary.note: Feminine noun; `bouillir` is the related verb.

vocabulary.example: Une pelouse commune est entretenue par la coopérative.
vocabulary.note: Feminine noun; `le gazon` names the grass itself.

vocabulary.example: Elle fait les magasins avec sa sœur le samedi après-midi.
vocabulary.note: Leisure shopping; groceries and errands are `faire les courses`.

vocabulary.example: Nous avons assisté à la séance d’information de mardi.
vocabulary.note: Assister à un événement means attend; the different construction assister quelqu’un means assist or help someone.

vocabulary.example: La garderie demande de ne pas apporter de jouet personnel.
vocabulary.note: Masculine noun; `un jeu` is a game, `un jouet` the object played with.

practice.prompt: Ask politely where the permits office is, then say it is on the first floor above the ground floor.
practice.hint: Use the request frame and the French floor word.
practice.answer: Pardon, où se trouve le service des permis, s’il vous plaît ? Il est au premier étage.

takeaways: `Pardon, où se trouve…, s’il vous plaît ?` is the reusable request.
`Rez-de-chaussée` equals ground floor; `premier étage` is above it.
Faire les courses usually covers groceries and necessities; shopping expressions can overlap.
keywords: le salon, un canapé, un sofa, un placard, un miroir, installer les meubles
un pinceau, le papier peint, un plafond, des rideaux, la douche
une cafetière, une bouilloire, la télévision, une caméra, un écran, le mot de passe, du wifi
un agenda, la monnaie, une bourse, un centre commercial
un quai, la consigne, un bagage, une tente, le camping, partir en vacances, un rang
