lessons.title: Les études, les consignes et les métiers
lessons.summary: Understand school stages, classroom subjects, learning instructions and professional roles. Distinguish taking an exam from administering it or passing successfully, and interpret occupational nouns in their context.
objectives: Recognise school stages without assuming that education systems are identical.
Follow common learning-interface and form instructions.
Name professions and distinguish a film director, a manager and a kitchen chef.

sections.title: School stages, subjects, and organised learning
paragraphs: `La maternelle (f.)`, short for `l’école maternelle (f.)`, is the preschool stage before primary school in France; translating it simply as kindergarten can hide differences between education systems. `Le lycée (m.)` is the upper-secondary school stage, not a university. `Une matière (f.)` is a school subject when talking about a timetable or studies; elsewhere it can mean material or substance.

`Une feuille (f.)` means a sheet in a classroom or paper context. `Un cours de musique (m.)` is a music class, while `un atelier de lecture (m.)` is a reading workshop with organised participation. `Des sujets actuels (m. pl.)` are current topics, not “actual” topics in contrast to imaginary ones.

`Faire passer un examen à quelqu’un` means administer an exam to someone. It describes the examiner's role; `passer un examen` describes the candidate taking it. Passing successfully is `réussir un examen`.
points: Read `matière` as subject when it belongs to a course programme.
Distinguish administering, taking, and successfully passing an exam.

examples.french: Sa fille est en maternelle et commencera l’école élémentaire l’an prochain.
examples.english: Her daughter is in preschool and will start elementary school next year.
examples.note: The French preschool stage.

examples.french: Il va au lycée et pense déjà à ses études après le bac.
examples.english: He attends upper-secondary school and is already thinking about his studies after the baccalaureate.
examples.note: `Le lycée` precedes higher education.

examples.french: Quelle matière préfères-tu au lycée : la géographie ou les mathématiques ?
examples.english: Which subject do you prefer at upper-secondary school: geography or mathematics?
examples.note: `Une matière` is an academic subject.

examples.french: Écrivez votre nom en haut de la feuille.
examples.english: Write your name at the top of the sheet.
examples.note: A sheet of paper, not a tree leaf.

examples.french: Elle suit un cours de musique et participe à des ateliers de lecture.
examples.english: She takes a music class and participates in reading workshops.
examples.note: A class and participatory workshops are different activity formats.

examples.french: Pendant l’atelier, nous discutons de sujets actuels comme le logement.
examples.english: During the workshop, we discuss current topics such as housing.
examples.note: `Actuels` means current or topical.

examples.french: L’enseignante fait passer un examen aux élèves ; ils espèrent tous le réussir.
examples.english: The teacher administers an exam to the pupils; they all hope to pass it.
examples.note: The examiner gives the exam; the pupils aim to succeed.

mistakes.avoid: J’ai fait passer l’examen.
mistakes.prefer: J’ai passé l’examen.
mistakes.why: If you were the candidate taking the exam, use passer. Faire passer is grammatical but places you in the examiner or administrator role.

mistakes.avoid: Nous discutons de sujets actuelle.
mistakes.prefer: Nous discutons de sujets actuels.
mistakes.why: Actuels agrees with masculine plural sujets and means current or topical. English actual is usually réel or véritable.

sections.title: Reading learning-interface instructions and form questions
paragraphs: `Cliquer sur` means click on a link, button, or item. `Consulter l’aide` means look at the help section or help documentation. `Compléter les phrases` means complete the sentences, often by supplying `les mots manquants`: the missing words. The headwords are `une phrase (f.)`, a sentence, and `un mot (m.)`, a word.

`Remettre les informations dans l’ordre` means put the information back into the required order. It is an ordering instruction, not a request to send information again. A personal-information form may ask whether someone is `marié/mariée`, married; the feminine form adds `-e`, but both describe marital status.
points: In a user interface, `l’aide (f.)` names help documentation, not necessarily a person helping you.
`Manquant/manquante` means missing; it identifies what must be supplied.

examples.french: Cliquez sur le lien pour ouvrir la leçon.
examples.english: Click the link to open the lesson.
examples.note: `Cliquer sur` names the selected interface item.

examples.french: Si vous ne comprenez pas la consigne, consultez l’aide.
examples.english: If you do not understand the instruction, consult the help section.
examples.note: A resource on the interface.

examples.french: Complétez les phrases avec les mots manquants.
examples.english: Complete the sentences with the missing words.
examples.note: The missing words are the content to add.

examples.french: Remettez les informations dans l’ordre de la vidéo.
examples.english: Put the information in the order in which it appears in the video.
examples.note: An ordering task, not resubmission.

examples.french: Le formulaire demande : « Êtes-vous marié ou mariée ? »
examples.english: The form asks, “Are you married?”
examples.note: The two written forms describe the respondent's marital status.

examples.french: Ma sœur est mariée, mais mon frère ne l’est pas.
examples.english: My sister is married, but my brother is not.
examples.note: Ordinary contextual use of the feminine form.

mistakes.avoid: Complétez les phrase avec les mots manquant.
mistakes.prefer: Complétez les phrases avec les mots manquants.
mistakes.why: Both phrases and mots are plural. The instruction asks you to supply the missing words.

sections.title: Writers, filmmakers, tradespeople, and managers
paragraphs: `Un écrivain (m.)` or `une écrivaine (f.)` is a writer, typically an author of literary works. `Une réalisatrice (f.)` or `un réalisateur (m.)` directs films or audiovisual work. That role is different from managing a business.

`Un pâtissier (m.)` or `une pâtissière (f.)` makes pastries professionally. `Un facteur (m.)` or `une factrice (f.)` delivers mail; the same masculine noun can mean a factor in a different context. `Un marchand (m.)` or `une marchande (f.)` is a merchant or seller, often identified by what they sell.

`Un chef (m.)` or `une cheffe (f.)` is a person in charge. The fuller phrase tells you the field: a team leader, department head, or kitchen chef. A bare `chef` in a workplace conversation need not have anything to do with cooking. After `être`, an unmodified occupation normally appears without an article, even though its noun headword has a gender.
points: Use `réalisateur/réalisatrice` for film directing, not as a universal translation of manager.
Interpret `chef` from the workplace and the complement, rather than assuming a kitchen.

examples.french: Cet écrivain publie son deuxième roman cette année.
examples.english: This writer is publishing his second novel this year.
examples.note: A literary author.

examples.french: La réalisatrice prépare un documentaire sur les écoles du quartier.
examples.english: The director is preparing a documentary about the neighbourhood’s schools.
examples.note: An audiovisual directing role.

examples.french: Nadia est pâtissière et prépare les desserts du restaurant.
examples.english: Nadia is a pastry chef and makes the restaurant’s desserts.
examples.note: A profession with no article after `est` in this sentence.

examples.french: Le pâtissier ouvre sa boutique à sept heures.
examples.english: The pastry chef opens his shop at seven.
examples.note: The masculine professional noun.

examples.french: La factrice distribue le courrier dans cette rue.
examples.english: The postal worker delivers the mail on this street.
examples.note: The feminine of the postal-worker noun `un facteur`.

examples.french: Ce marchand vend des tissus au marché.
examples.english: This merchant sells fabrics at the market.
examples.note: The verb and object identify what the seller trades.

examples.french: Ma cheffe d’équipe répartit les tâches entre quatre collègues.
examples.english: My team leader divides the tasks among four colleagues.
examples.note: A managerial role, not a cook.

mistakes.avoid: Un factrice distribue le courrier.
mistakes.prefer: Une factrice distribue le courrier.
mistakes.why: Factrice is the feminine professional noun and takes une.

mistakes.avoid: Les pâtissier préparent les desserts.
mistakes.prefer: Les pâtissiers préparent les desserts.
mistakes.why: The plural noun pâtissiers takes -s. A team leader is un chef d’équipe or une cheffe d’équipe, not necessarily a cook.

vocabulary.english: a school subject; material or substance in other contexts
vocabulary.example: La géographie est ma matière préférée.
vocabulary.note: The school context selects the subject meaning.

vocabulary.example: La factrice distribue le courrier.
vocabulary.note: Feminine of un facteur (m.) in the postal-worker sense.

practice.prompt: Say that you took an exam yesterday and passed it.
practice.hint: Taking it and succeeding require two different verbs.
practice.answer: J’ai passé un examen hier et je l’ai réussi.

takeaways: Compare education systems before translating a school stage.
Passer, faire passer and réussir un examen describe different roles or outcomes.
Use the full occupational phrase to identify the role.
keywords: school education classroom learning instructions professions jobs

un cours de musique un atelier de lecture sujets actuels
faire passer un examen passer réussir
cliquer consulter l’aide compléter les phrases les mots manquants
remettre les informations dans l’ordre marié mariée formulaire
un écrivain une écrivaine une réalisatrice un réalisateur
un pâtissier une pâtissière un facteur une factrice un marchand

lessons.title: Les nouvelles, les médias et la vie collective
lessons.summary: Distinguish broadcast news, a piece of news and personal updates. Describe solidarity and public events precisely without confusing solidarity with solitude or every demonstration with a riot.
objectives: Distinguish les informations, une nouvelle and des nouvelles in context.
Use solidaire de for solidarity, not solitude.
Describe public events without exaggerating their nature.

sections.title: News, solidarity, and community experience
paragraphs: Les informations (f. pl.) can mean the news, especially a radio or television news programme. Outside that context, the same noun refers to information. Une nouvelle (f.) is a piece of news, and les nouvelles (f. pl.) can be public news or updates about a person. These are nouns, unlike the adjective nouvelle in une nouvelle proposition.

Solidaire means showing solidarity or standing together with others, often in être solidaire de quelqu’un. It is not the English word solitary. Une émeute (f.) is a riot involving violent public disorder, not a neutral synonym for any demonstration. Une manifestation (f.) is a demonstration; describe what happened rather than assuming that every gathering was violent.
points: Regarder les informations usually means watch the news.
Demander des nouvelles de quelqu’un asks how someone is doing.
Distinguish a peaceful demonstration from a riot, and solidarity from solitude.

examples.french: Je regarde les informations pour suivre les décisions qui concernent notre quartier.
examples.english: I watch the news to follow decisions affecting our neighbourhood.
examples.note: The broadcast-news sense.

examples.french: La bonne nouvelle, c’est que le centre restera ouvert.
examples.english: The good news is that the centre will remain open.
examples.note: Une nouvelle is a news item, not the adjective new.

examples.french: Avez-vous des nouvelles de votre ancienne collègue ?
examples.english: Have you heard any news of your former colleague?
examples.note: Personal updates rather than a news programme.

examples.french: Nous sommes solidaires des familles qui ont perdu leur logement.
examples.english: We stand in solidarity with the families who lost their homes.
examples.note: Solidaires de expresses support and shared concern; de + les becomes des.

examples.french: Après l’émeute, notre association a aidé les commerçants dont les magasins avaient été endommagés.
examples.english: After the riot, our association helped the shopkeepers whose shops had been damaged.
examples.note: A specific description of community support after a violent event.

examples.french: La manifestation est restée pacifique ; ce n’était pas une émeute.
examples.english: The demonstration remained peaceful; it was not a riot.
examples.note: The words do not describe the same kind of event.

mistakes.avoid: Avez-vous des nouvelle de ma sœur ?
mistakes.prefer: Avez-vous des nouvelles de ma sœur ?
mistakes.why: The expression avoir des nouvelles de quelqu’un uses the plural nouvelles: news or updates about someone.

mistakes.avoid: Je suis solidaire.
mistakes.prefer: Je suis seul / seule.
mistakes.why: If you intend I am alone, use seul or seule. Je suis solidaire is grammatical but expresses solidarity, not solitude.

vocabulary.example: J’ai une bonne nouvelle à vous annoncer.
vocabulary.note: A countable news item; English news itself is normally uncountable.

vocabulary.example: La manifestation s’est déroulée dans le calme.
vocabulary.note: Does not by itself imply a riot.

practice.prompt: Ask a friend whether they have heard from a former colleague.
practice.hint: Use avoir des nouvelles de quelqu’un.
practice.answer: As-tu des nouvelles de notre ancienne collègue ?

takeaways: News vocabulary changes meaning with the context.
Solidaire de expresses solidarity; seul/seule expresses being alone.
Choose a public-event noun that matches what actually happened.

modules.title: Rédiger des messages et des textes
modules.description: Write courteous requests, personal messages, job applications and reasoned arguments, with complete models and a tone suited to the reader.

lessons.title: La cohésion et le registre formel
lessons.summary: Write clear, courteous messages with a stated purpose, logical links and a specific request. Keep standard written negation and choose a tone suited to the recipient. A professional email can be concise; longer letter formulas are options, not requirements for every message.
objectives: Open a formal message by naming its purpose and its context.
Link ideas with connectors of cause, consequence, and contrast.
Close with a conventional request and politeness formula.

sections.title: Core concept
paragraphs: Cohesion means the links that make a text easy to follow; register is the level of formality suited to the reader and situation. In standard formal writing, retain ne in ordinary verb negation: je ne peux pas. Avoid markedly conversational forms such as ouais or un resto when the context calls for a formal tone. Not every shortened word is informal: a photo, le métro and un CV can be appropriate. Clear pronoun references, consistent tenses and paragraph order matter as much as connectors.

Choose a connector for the relationship you actually mean: car introduces a reason, en effet can explain or confirm the preceding point, par conséquent marks a consequence, cependant marks a contrast and en outre adds information. Et remains correct in formal writing; do not replace every occurrence or insert a connector where the link is already clear.

For a request, identify the purpose and any useful reference, give the relevant facts, then ask for a specific action. Pourriez-vous me confirmer la date ? is suitable in many professional emails. Je vous prie de bien vouloir… is a more ceremonious option, not the only polite request. A short closing such as Cordialement may suit an email; a formal letter may call for Je vous prie d’agréer, Madame, Monsieur, mes salutations distinguées. Match the formula to the relationship and medium.

Do not make writing heavier just to sound formal. Faire une demande and faire le nécessaire are valid professional expressions. Effectuer une vérification or réaliser une étude can be more precise in the right combination, but these verbs are not interchangeable replacements for every faire.
points: State the purpose and the reference in the first sentence.
Use standard written negation and avoid vocabulary that is too casual for the recipient.
Choose connectors for meaning; use et where simple addition is all you need.
Make a clear, polite request; choose a concise or ceremonial form to fit the situation.
Proofread articles, agreements, accents, and verb complements before sending.
Use precise natural combinations, not longer words for their own sake. Un texte soigné highlights care and polish.

examples.french: Je vous écris au sujet de l’offre publiée le 3 mars afin de vous soumettre ma candidature.
examples.english: I am writing regarding the position advertised on 3 March in order to submit my application.
examples.note: Opening that states purpose and reference.

examples.french: Je vous prie de bien vouloir examiner ma candidature.
examples.english: I would be grateful if you would consider my application.
examples.note: Standard courteous request formula.

examples.french: Mon dossier était incomplet ; par conséquent, je vous transmets aujourd’hui les pièces manquantes.
examples.english: My file was incomplete; consequently, I am sending you the missing documents today.
examples.note: Explicit consequence connector.

examples.french: Si cela était possible, j’aimerais également savoir quand les entretiens auraient lieu.
examples.english: If that were possible, I would also like to know when the interviews would take place.
examples.note: Conditional forms soften a second request.

examples.french: Je vous prie d’agréer, Madame, Monsieur, mes salutations distinguées.
examples.english: Yours faithfully.
examples.note: Conventional closing formula for a formal letter.

examples.french: Nous avons effectué les vérifications demandées et réalisé une nouvelle estimation.
examples.english: We carried out the requested checks and produced a new estimate.
examples.note: Natural combinations here; faire les vérifications would also be acceptable.

examples.french: Bonjour, je vous contacte au sujet de mon inscription du 12 juin. Je n’ai pas reçu de confirmation. Pourriez-vous vérifier mon dossier et me préciser la date de début du cours ? Je vous remercie de votre aide. Cordialement, Alex Martin.
examples.english: Hello, I am contacting you about my registration of 12 June. I have not received a confirmation. Could you check my file and let me know the course start date? Thank you for your help. Kind regards, Alex Martin.
examples.note: A complete concise email: purpose, relevant fact, specific request and courteous closing. In an email, separate the greeting, body and closing into paragraphs.

mistakes.avoid: Je peux pas venir le 12, mais je vous prie de bien vouloir examiner mon dossier.
mistakes.prefer: Je ne peux pas venir le 12, mais je vous prie de bien vouloir examiner mon dossier.
mistakes.why: Formal writing keeps `ne`; dropping it belongs to informal speech.

mistakes.avoid: Je veux bien que vous examinez mon dossier avant vendredi.
mistakes.prefer: Je veux bien que vous examiniez mon dossier avant vendredi.
mistakes.why: `Vouloir que` is a subjunctive trigger, so the verb is `examiniez`, not the indicative `examinez`; in a formal request, `Je vous prie de bien vouloir examiner` is better still.

mistakes.avoid: J’ai envoyé le dossier et il était incomplet et j’ai envoyé les pièces.
mistakes.prefer: J’ai envoyé le dossier, mais il était incomplet ; c’est pourquoi je vous transmets les pièces manquantes.
mistakes.why: The first version is grammatical but repetitive and vague about the links. Mais identifies the problem; c’est pourquoi connects it to the action.

vocabulary.example: Une candidature complète doit inclure une lettre de motivation.
vocabulary.note: Feminine noun; `poser sa candidature` means to apply.

vocabulary.example: Une lettre de motivation d’une page suffit pour ce poste.
vocabulary.note: Feminine noun phrase; the gender comes from `lettre`.

vocabulary.french: je vous prie de bien vouloir
vocabulary.english: I would be grateful if you would
vocabulary.example: Je vous prie de bien vouloir me confirmer la date de l’entretien.
vocabulary.note: A ceremonial request frame followed by an infinitive; a concise Pourriez-vous… may suit an ordinary professional email.

vocabulary.example: Le délai est dépassé ; par conséquent, une nouvelle demande est nécessaire.
vocabulary.note: Formal connector of consequence; `donc` is its neutral equivalent.

vocabulary.example: Un entretien bien préparé permet de présenter ses compétences avec assurance.
vocabulary.note: Un entretien (m.) can mean an interview; une entrevue (f.) is also common in Canada.

vocabulary.example: Le service effectue une vérification avant chaque versement.
vocabulary.note: Formal equivalent of `faire` with a process or an operation.

vocabulary.example: Une lettre soignée fait une meilleure impression qu’un texte rapide.
vocabulary.note: Soigné highlights care and finish. Propre can mean clean or neat; choose the word for the quality you actually mean.

practice.prompt: Write the opening sentence of a formal message asking for an appointment about a housing application.
practice.hint: Name the purpose and the reference before making the request.
practice.answer: Je vous écris au sujet de ma demande de logement déposée le 12 février, afin de solliciter un rendez-vous avec un conseiller.

takeaways: Purpose first, one reason per paragraph, explicit request last.
Use standard written negation and vocabulary suited to the reader.
Choose a clear request and a closing suited to an email or a formal letter.

lessons.title: Le récit d’un déménagement et la description d’un quartier
lessons.summary: A personal narrative can use the compound past for the move, the imperfect for background conditions, and the present for the current assessment. `S’habituer à` describes adaptation; `y` can replace a known thing in `je m’y suis habitué`, without making alternatives such as `je me suis habitué à ça` wrong. Evaluations use `ce que j’aime le plus`, `ce qui manque`, and `il y a`.
objectives: Introduce the move as a completed event.
Describe the initial situation with the imperfect.
Evaluate the neighbourhood in the present with a clear structure.

sections.title: Core concept
paragraphs: One useful narrative route is the move, the initial situation, then your present experience. Use the passé composé for a completed event: J’ai déménagé à Montréal il y a quelques semaines. Use the imparfait for background viewed as ongoing: Au début, c’était difficile, je ne connaissais personne. This is a writing plan, not a fixed tense formula: Ça a été difficile presents a bounded difficult period, while Je m’habitue encore au quartier describes adaptation that is still happening.

For your current assessment, Ce que j’aime le plus ici, c’est que… highlights a strength; ce qui manque encore, c’est… names a gap; il y a and on trouve introduce amenities. S’habituer à takes à, and y can replace a known non-person complement: Je m’y suis habitué. Keeping the complement is also grammatical: Je me suis habitué à ça. For a person, use a stressed pronoun: Je me suis habitué à elle. In these examples, a speaker using feminine agreement writes habituée.

Choose details that help the reader understand your experience: transport, the rent, nearby services or a specific encounter. Une rue (f.) can be étroite, meaning narrow; un quartier (m.) can be animé or calme. Une garderie accessible is not automatically an affordable daycare: accessible can concern location, availability or physical access. To specify price, write une garderie à un prix abordable.
points: Open with the completed move in the compound past.
Set the initial difficulty or context in the imperfect.
Choose the tense of s’habituer à according to whether adaptation is complete, ongoing now or background in the past.
Use `y` to avoid repeating a known thing after `à`; replacement is optional.
Evaluate in the present with `ce que j’aime le plus, c’est que…`.
Describe the outside of a building with `une façade` and any wall, inside or out, with `un mur`.
Describe a neighbourhood with `animé`, `calme`, `étroit`, and name what disrupts it, such as `la circulation` or `une panne d’électricité`.

examples.french: J’ai déménagé à Montréal il y a quelques semaines pour me rapprocher de mon travail.
examples.english: I moved to Montreal a few weeks ago to be closer to my job.
examples.note: Completed event in the compound past.

examples.french: Au début, c’était difficile : je ne connaissais personne et le loyer était élevé.
examples.english: At first it was difficult: I did not know anyone and the rent was high.
examples.note: Initial conditions in the imperfect.

examples.french: Je me suis habitué au quartier, et maintenant je m’y sens chez moi.
examples.english: I got used to the neighbourhood, and now I feel at home there.
examples.note: Completed change of state, then « y » for a known place.

examples.french: Ce que j’aime le plus ici, c’est qu’il y a beaucoup de services de proximité.
examples.english: What I like most here is that there are many local services.
examples.note: Ready-made frame for a positive evaluation.

examples.french: Ce qui manque encore, c’est une garderie accessible près de la station de métro.
examples.english: What is still missing is an accessible daycare near the subway station.
examples.note: Accessible does not specify price by itself. Use à un prix abordable if affordability is what you mean.

examples.french: La façade de l’immeuble a été rénovée, mais les murs intérieurs restent à peindre.
examples.english: The front of the building has been renovated, but the interior walls still have to be painted.
examples.note: « Une façade » is the outward face of a building; « un mur » is any wall.

examples.french: Le quartier est animé le jour, mais les rues étroites et la circulation compliquent le stationnement.
examples.english: The neighbourhood is lively during the day, but the narrow streets and the traffic make parking difficult.
examples.note: Evaluation adjectives plus the noun naming the difficulty.

examples.french: Je vous écris au sujet d’une panne d’électricité qui a touché l’immeuble ainsi que les commerces voisins.
examples.english: I am writing about a power outage that affected the building as well as the neighbouring shops.
examples.note: Au sujet de introduces the subject of this message; ainsi que adds a second element.

examples.french: Salut Nora ! J’ai déménagé à Montréal le mois dernier. Au début, je me perdais dans le métro, mais une voisine m’a aidé à trouver mes repères. Maintenant, je vais au travail en vingt minutes. Le quartier me plaît, même si le loyer est un peu élevé. Tu viendras le découvrir samedi ?
examples.english: Hi Nora! I moved to Montreal last month. At first, I kept getting lost on the subway, but a neighbour helped me find my bearings. Now I get to work in twenty minutes. I like the neighbourhood, although the rent is a little high. Will you come and see it on Saturday?
examples.note: A connected informal message for a speaker using masculine agreement in aidé. It combines a dated move, background, a helpful event, a current assessment and an invitation.

mistakes.avoid: Au début, c’étais difficile et je ne connaissait personne.
mistakes.prefer: Au début, c’était difficile et je ne connaissais personne.
mistakes.why: Use third-person `était` in c’était and first-person `connaissais` with je. The imperfect presents background; a compound past can instead present a bounded episode.

mistakes.avoid: Je me suis habitué le quartier rapidement.
mistakes.prefer: Je me suis habitué au quartier rapidement.
mistakes.why: `S’habituer` requires the preposition `à`, contracted here to `au`.

mistakes.avoid: Nous avons repeint les mur de la cuisine le mois dernier.
mistakes.prefer: Nous avons repeint les murs de la cuisine le mois dernier.
mistakes.why: After plural `les`, write the regular noun plural `murs`.

vocabulary.example: Elle s’est habituée à l’hiver canadien après deux saisons.
vocabulary.note: Takes à; y can replace a known thing, but keeping the complement is also grammatical.

vocabulary.example: Un quartier animé offre de nombreux commerces de proximité.
vocabulary.note: Masculine noun; `de proximité` means local or nearby.

vocabulary.example: Un commerce de proximité vient d’ouvrir près de la station de métro.
vocabulary.note: Masculine noun phrase; the gender comes from `commerce`.

vocabulary.example: Un loyer raisonnable reste difficile à trouver dans ce secteur.
vocabulary.note: Masculine noun; `louer` is the related verb.

vocabulary.example: Un logement lumineux facilite l’installation de toute la famille.
vocabulary.note: Masculine noun and the standard administrative term; the feeling of home is `un chez-soi`.

vocabulary.example: Un mur mitoyen sépare les deux logements.
vocabulary.note: Masculine noun; used for interior and exterior walls alike.

vocabulary.example: Une façade bien entretenue améliore l’image de tout le quartier.
vocabulary.note: Feminine noun; only the outward face of a building.

vocabulary.example: La circulation est dense sur ce boulevard aux heures de pointe.
vocabulary.note: Feminine noun; it also means circulation in a medical sense.

vocabulary.example: Un quai couvert protège les voyageurs pendant l’hiver.
vocabulary.note: Masculine noun; used for both a station platform and a waterfront.

vocabulary.example: La campagne est plus calme, mais les services y sont plus éloignés.
vocabulary.note: Feminine noun; `une campagne` also means a campaign.

vocabulary.example: Une panne d’électricité a duré trois heures dans tout le secteur.
vocabulary.note: Feminine noun phrase; the gender comes from `panne`.

vocabulary.example: Une rue animée rassure les résidents le soir.
vocabulary.note: Describes a place full of activity; the opposite here is `calme`.

vocabulary.example: Une rue étroite complique le passage des camions de livraison.
vocabulary.note: Regular feminine in `-e`; the opposite is `large`.

vocabulary.example: Je vous écris au sujet du bruit nocturne dans notre immeuble.
vocabulary.note: Formal alternative to `à propos de` in written requests.

vocabulary.example: Le quartier compte deux écoles ainsi qu’une bibliothèque municipale.
vocabulary.note: Here ainsi que joins objects; compte agrees with the singular subject le quartier. When ainsi que joins subjects in an additive sense, the verb normally takes the plural.

practice.prompt: Write three sentences: the move, the initial difficulty, and what you like most now.
practice.hint: Compound past, imperfect, then the present with a fixed frame.
practice.answer: J’ai déménagé à Laval en janvier. Au début, c’était difficile parce que je ne connaissais pas les transports. Ce que j’aime le plus ici, c’est qu’il y a une bibliothèque et une clinique tout près.

takeaways: Move in the compound past, background in the imperfect, assessment in the present.
`S’habituer à` plus `y` for a known place.
`Ce que j’aime le plus, c’est que…` is reusable in any evaluation.
keywords: describing a move and a neighbourhood

lessons.title: La présentation d’une candidature
lessons.summary: Present an application with a clear purpose, relevant experience and concrete evidence. Use postuler un poste or poser sa candidature; postuler à/pour un poste is also accepted by the OQLF. Choose tenses for the actual time and meaning, and use polite phrasing without making every claim hypothetical.
objectives: Use the correct French verbs for applying.
Name the position and match it with relevant experience.
Distinguish facts, earlier responsibilities, proposals and polite requests.

sections.title: Core concept
paragraphs: To apply for a job, you can say postuler un poste, poser sa candidature à un poste or soumettre sa candidature. The OQLF also accepts postuler à/pour un emploi. Usage recommendations differ: the Académie française prefers the direct construction postuler un emploi. Do not treat the direct object as an error. Poser sa candidature is a useful alternative across these recommendations. Avoid appliquer pour un emploi in standard French; appliquer is used for such actions as applying a rule, a method or paint.

Choose tense for the meaning, not because the text is an application. Use the passé composé for a completed achievement: J’ai coordonné une équipe de six personnes. Use the present for a current situation: Je travaille actuellement dans un organisme communautaire. The imparfait can describe previous responsibilities: Dans mon ancien poste, je gérais les inscriptions. A conditional can express a proposal, a hypothesis or politeness; it is not restricted to the closing. Je suis disponible dès lundi states confirmed availability, while Je serais disponible… can make it conditional on arrangements.

Name the position, connect a relevant skill to an actual task or result, and explain the contribution you could make. State your experience honestly; do not invent achievements or figures to sound convincing. The following models are fictional language examples, not claims to copy into your own application.
points: Say `postuler à` or `poser sa candidature à`, never `appliquer`.
Name the exact position and where you saw it advertised.
Use the compound past for achievements and the present for current skills.
Distinguish confirmed facts from proposals, conditions and polite requests.
Match every claim with a concrete example rather than an adjective.

examples.french: J’ai posé ma candidature à ce poste de coordonnateur la semaine dernière.
examples.english: I applied for this coordinator position last week.
examples.note: Completed action in the compound past.

examples.french: Je travaille actuellement dans un organisme communautaire et je coordonne trois bénévoles.
examples.english: I currently work for a community organisation and I coordinate three volunteers.
examples.note: Present tense for a current situation.

examples.french: Mon expérience en milieu associatif correspond au profil recherché dans votre annonce.
examples.english: My experience in the non-profit sector matches the profile described in your advertisement.
examples.note: A claim linked directly to the advertisement.

examples.french: Si j’obtenais ce poste, je pourrais mettre en place un suivi bilingue des dossiers.
examples.english: If I obtained this position, I could set up bilingual case follow-up.
examples.note: The conditional used for a genuine hypothesis.

examples.french: Je serais disponible pour un entretien à partir du 1er mai.
examples.english: I would be available for an interview from 1 May.
examples.note: The conditional leaves availability tentative or dependent on arrangements. Je suis disponible… states confirmed availability.

examples.french: Madame, Monsieur, je souhaite poser ma candidature au poste d’agent d’accueil. Dans mon précédent emploi, je gérais les inscriptions et renseignais les visiteurs. J’ai également créé un guide bilingue pour répondre aux questions fréquentes. Je serais heureux de mettre cette expérience au service de votre équipe. Vous trouverez mon CV en pièce jointe.
examples.english: Dear Sir or Madam, I would like to apply for the receptionist position. In my previous job, I handled registrations and provided information to visitors. I also created a bilingual guide to answer frequently asked questions. I would be happy to put this experience to use for your team. You will find my CV attached.
examples.note: A fictional connected model for a speaker using masculine heureux: position, past responsibilities, completed achievement, proposed contribution and attachment. Replace the experience with your own; heureuse is the feminine form.

mistakes.avoid: J’ai appliqué pour ce poste la semaine dernière.
mistakes.prefer: J’ai posé ma candidature à ce poste la semaine dernière.
mistakes.why: In standard French, applying for a job is poser sa candidature or postuler, not appliquer pour. The passé composé presents the completed application.

mistakes.avoid: J’ai poser ma candidature hier.
mistakes.prefer: J’ai posé ma candidature hier.
mistakes.why: After ai in the passé composé, use the past participle posé, not the infinitive poser. J’ai postulé ce poste is also grammatically valid.

sections.title: Describe careful research and planning
paragraphs: `La recherche (f.)` means research when describing systematic investigation. `Une source (f.)` is a source of evidence or information. `Évaluer` means evaluate or assess, rather than merely think about something. `Un discours (m.)` is a speech or an extended public address; it does not automatically mean a conversation.

`Être conscient/consciente de` means be aware of something. With a following statement, use `être conscient que`. This is awareness, not conscientiousness: someone who works conscientiously is `consciencieux/consciencieuse`. `Planifier` means plan or schedule, and `avec soin` means carefully, with attention.

`Regarder les e-mails` can mean check emails in everyday speech. `Consulter ses e-mails` or `consulter sa messagerie` is more precise in a professional description. If the task is checking their accuracy, use `vérifier` and say what you verify.
points: Show what you assessed or planned instead of using `évaluer` or `planifier` without context.
Keep awareness (`conscient de`) separate from diligence (`consciencieux`).

examples.french: Dans mon travail de recherche, j’évalue la fiabilité de chaque source.
examples.english: In my research work, I assess the reliability of each source.
examples.note: Research, evaluation, and evidence sources in one task.

examples.french: J’ai préparé un discours pour présenter les résultats à l’équipe.
examples.english: I prepared a speech to present the results to the team.
examples.note: A prepared address, not a casual exchange.

examples.french: Je suis consciente des difficultés rencontrées par les nouveaux arrivants.
examples.english: I am aware of the difficulties faced by newcomers.
examples.note: `Des` represents `de + les` after `consciente`.

examples.french: Je suis conscient que ce changement demande du temps.
examples.english: I am aware that this change takes time.
examples.note: A statement follows `que` instead of a noun following `de`.

examples.french: Je planifie les réunions et prépare chaque dossier avec soin.
examples.english: I schedule the meetings and prepare each file carefully.
examples.note: Concrete responsibilities plus careful execution.

examples.french: Chaque matin, je consulte ma messagerie et je classe les demandes par ordre de priorité.
examples.english: Every morning, I check my email inbox and sort requests by priority.
examples.note: A concrete work routine. Je regarde mes e-mails is also possible in everyday speech.

mistakes.avoid: Je suis conscient.
mistakes.prefer: Je suis consciencieux dans mon travail.
mistakes.why: If you mean I am conscientious in my work, use consciencieux. The first sentence is grammatical but can mean I am conscious; conscient de means aware of.

mistakes.avoid: J’évalue le problème.
mistakes.prefer: Je réfléchis au problème.
mistakes.why: If you only mean I am thinking about the problem, use réfléchir à. Évaluer is grammatical but adds the meaning of assessment, such as estimating cost or importance.

sections.title: Employment, future plans, and approval
paragraphs: `Employer quelqu’un` means employ someone, having that person work for an organisation or person. It can overlap with hire, but `embaucher` or `engager` makes the act of recruitment explicit. This is different from `employer un mot`, to use a word.

`L’avenir (m.)` means the future, especially prospects or what lies ahead. `Un enjeu (m.)`, plural `des enjeux (m. pl.)`, is what is at stake, or an important issue or challenge within a decision. It is not just any minor problem. `Soutenir` means support a person, proposal, or activity; the context tells you whether that support is practical, moral, or financial.

`Un aval (m.)` is approval or backing, often in administrative or professional language. Common expressions are `donner son aval` and `obtenir l’aval de quelqu’un`. Approval is more specific than general encouragement.
points: Person employed: `employer quelqu’un`. Tool or word used: `employer quelque chose`.
Name what matters when describing `les enjeux`: jobs, access, funding, safety, or another concrete concern.

examples.french: Cette association emploie douze personnes à temps plein.
examples.english: This association employs twelve people full-time.
examples.note: An ongoing employment relationship.

examples.french: L’entreprise prévoit d’embaucher deux personnes et pourra ainsi employer une équipe plus nombreuse.
examples.english: The company plans to hire two people and will thus be able to employ a larger team.
examples.note: `Embaucher` focuses on hiring; `employer` on having staff.

examples.french: Je souhaite construire mon avenir professionnel dans ce secteur.
examples.english: I would like to build my professional future in this sector.
examples.note: Future prospects, not a grammatical tense.

examples.french: L’avenir du service est un enjeu important pour les habitants.
examples.english: The future of the service is an important issue for the residents.
examples.note: Something consequential is at stake.

examples.french: Nous avons expliqué les enjeux du projet avant de demander un financement.
examples.english: We explained what was at stake in the project before requesting funding.
examples.note: `Les enjeux` identifies the significant issues and consequences.

examples.french: J’ai soutenu mes collègues pendant la réorganisation.
examples.english: I supported my colleagues during the reorganisation.
examples.note: Support for people, without claiming that the support was necessarily financial.

examples.french: Nous avons obtenu l’aval de la direction avant de lancer le projet.
examples.english: We obtained management’s approval before launching the project.
examples.note: Formal approval or backing.

mistakes.avoid: Cette association emploient douze personnes.
mistakes.prefer: Cette association emploie douze personnes.
mistakes.why: Emploie agrees with singular cette association. Here employer means employ staff, not merely use people.

mistakes.avoid: Nous avons obtenu la aval de la direction.
mistakes.prefer: Nous avons obtenu l’aval de la direction.
mistakes.why: Aval is masculine and begins with a vowel: le elides to l’. Obtenir l’aval means obtain approval or backing.

vocabulary.example: Je postule à ce poste de coordonnateur bilingue.
vocabulary.note: The OQLF accepts postuler à/pour un emploi and the direct postuler un emploi; the latter is preferred by the Académie française.

vocabulary.example: Elle a posé sa candidature à trois offres publiées cette semaine.
vocabulary.note: Followed by `à` or `pour` plus the position.

vocabulary.example: Un poste à temps plein a été affiché sur le site de la ville.
vocabulary.note: Masculine for a position; la poste (f.) names the postal service, and un bureau de poste (m.) is a post office.

vocabulary.example: Une annonce détaillée précise les compétences attendues.
vocabulary.note: Feminine noun; `une offre d’emploi` is the fuller term.

vocabulary.example: Une compétence en gestion de projet est demandée pour ce poste.
vocabulary.note: Feminine noun; usually plural when listing skills.

practice.prompt: Write one sentence naming the position you are applying for and one relevant piece of experience.
practice.hint: Use `postuler à` or `poser sa candidature` and the compound past.
practice.answer: Je pose ma candidature au poste d’agent d’accueil, car j’ai travaillé deux ans dans un centre de services aux nouveaux arrivants.

takeaways: `Postuler à` and `poser sa candidature`, never `appliquer`.
Compound past for achievements, present for current skills.
Tense and mood express the time and meaning, not a fixed application template.
keywords: un discours, la recherche, évaluer, une source, être conscient de, planifier, avec soin
regarder les e-mails, consulter ses e-mails, l’avenir, un enjeu, des enjeux, soutenir, employer

lessons.title: Construire une argumentation efficace
lessons.summary: Answer the question with a clear position or comparison, explain your reasons, and distinguish real evidence from hypothetical examples. Use concession and focus structures when they help the argument; do not invent statistics or add complex grammar merely to sound advanced.
objectives: State a defensible position that answers the exact question.
Support each reason with a concrete example or consequence.
Focus a sentence with the three cleft structures.
Close with a recommendation and its expected result.

sections.title: Core concept
paragraphs: A useful structure is position, support, a relevant limitation, then conclusion. Adapt it to the question: some tasks ask for a balanced comparison rather than a simple choice of sides. Make a specific claim and explain why it follows from an example, evidence or a plausible consequence. A personal preference alone is not evidence that a measure benefits everyone.

Use real, relevant information when it is available. Never invent a statistic or present an imagined example as a documented result. A hypothetical example is useful when labelled as such: Par exemple, un bus supplémentaire à huit heures pourrait réduire l’attente. Explain the connection between your example and your claim; greater ridership by itself does not prove lower pollution.

A concession acknowledges a real limitation before you qualify or defend the proposal: Certes, augmenter la fréquence des bus coûterait plus cher, mais un essai limité permettrait d’en évaluer l’utilité. You need not insert a concession into every short paragraph. A conclusion may recommend an action or simply answer the question. Useful purpose and evaluation frames include il est important que, il faudrait que and afin que, followed by the subjunctive.

Three cleft structures let you focus a sentence. `Ce que… c’est…` uses `ce que` as the following verb’s object: `Ce que j’apprécie le plus dans ce quartier, c’est la proximité des commerces`. `Ce qui… c’est…` uses `ce qui` as its subject: `Ce qui me préoccupe, c’est le coût du logement`. `C’est… qui…` and `C’est… que…` isolate a phrase: `C’est la bibliothèque qui a transformé le quartier`. Choose the relative pronoun by its grammatical function. When listing several benefits, parallel noun phrases can make the sentence easier to follow; that is a clarity recommendation, not a ban on every combination of different structures.

Environmental and public-service topics recur often, and precise words help. Clean air is `l’air pur` (masculine); air quality is `la qualité de l’air` (feminine). `L’eau potable` means drinking water, whereas `l’eau claire` describes clear water without guaranteeing that it is safe to drink. Useful frames include `À mon avis, il est nécessaire de…`, `Si l’air est trop pollué, les gens peuvent tomber malades`, and `De nos jours, le transport en commun réduit la pollution`, each stating a position or a consequence.
points: Answer the exact question in the first sentence, taking a side.
Develop one reason per paragraph or speaking segment.
Attach every reason to an example, a figure, or a consequence.
Use `certes… mais` to concede and answer an objection.
Close with a recommendation proportionate to the argument.
Describe a trend with `grimper`, `augmenter`, `baisser`, or `diminuer` before drawing a conclusion from it.
Focus an object with `Ce que… c’est…` and a subject with `Ce qui… c’est…`.
Use C’est… qui… for a focused subject; use C’est… que… for a focused object or adverbial phrase, retaining any needed preposition: C’est à la mairie que je vais.
Prefer parallel phrases when listing benefits after c’est, for ease of reading.
Write `l’air pur` for clean air and `l’eau potable` for drinking water.

examples.french: Selon moi, la ville devrait investir davantage dans le transport en commun.
examples.english: In my view, the city should invest more in public transit.
examples.note: A clear position stated at the outset.

examples.french: Des bus plus fréquents pourraient encourager certains automobilistes à changer leurs habitudes.
examples.english: More frequent buses could encourage some drivers to change their habits.
examples.note: A plausible mechanism stated cautiously, not an automatic guarantee of reduced pollution.

examples.french: Par exemple, un bus supplémentaire à huit heures pourrait réduire l’attente devant la gare.
examples.english: For example, an additional bus at eight o’clock could reduce the wait outside the station.
examples.note: A clearly hypothetical example, not an invented statistic presented as measured evidence.

examples.french: Certes, augmenter la fréquence des bus coûterait plus cher, mais un essai limité permettrait d’en évaluer l’utilité.
examples.english: Admittedly, increasing bus frequency would cost more, but a limited trial would make it possible to assess its usefulness.
examples.note: A limitation followed by a proportionate way to investigate the proposal.

examples.french: Il est important que les nouveaux arrivants se sentent les bienvenus dans leur quartier.
examples.english: It is important that newcomers feel welcome in their neighbourhood.
examples.note: The impersonal frame triggers the subjunctive.

examples.french: En conclusion, il faudrait étendre le réseau progressivement afin que chaque quartier en bénéficie.
examples.english: In conclusion, the network should be extended gradually so that every neighbourhood benefits.
examples.note: Recommendation plus purpose clause in the subjunctive.

examples.french: Ce que j’apprécie le plus dans ce quartier, c’est la proximité des commerces et des services publics.
examples.english: What I appreciate most in this neighbourhood is how close the shops and public services are.
examples.note: « Ce que » because the focused element is the object of « apprécier ».

examples.french: Ce qui me préoccupe, c’est le coût du logement pour les jeunes familles.
examples.english: What worries me is the cost of housing for young families.
examples.note: « Ce qui » because the focused element is the subject of « préoccuper ».

examples.french: C’est la bibliothèque municipale qui a transformé la vie du quartier.
examples.english: It is the municipal library that transformed life in the neighbourhood.
examples.note: « C’est… qui » isolates and highlights the subject.

examples.french: À mon avis, il est nécessaire de protéger l’air pur et de garantir l’eau potable à tous les quartiers.
examples.english: In my view, it is necessary to protect clean air and to guarantee drinking water for every neighbourhood.
examples.note: « L’air pur » for clean air and « l’eau potable » for drinking water.

mistakes.avoid: Je pense que ce soit une bonne mesure pour le quartier.
mistakes.prefer: Je pense que c’est une bonne mesure pour le quartier.
mistakes.why: Affirmative penser que normally takes the indicative when stating a belief. Negative or interrogative forms can use the subjunctive when the idea is uncertain or not asserted; they do not automatically require it in every context.

mistakes.avoid: Il est important que la ville investit davantage dans les transports.
mistakes.prefer: Il est important que la ville investisse davantage dans les transports.
mistakes.why: `Il est important que` is a subjunctive trigger.

mistakes.avoid: Ce qui j’aime dans ce quartier, c’est le calme.
mistakes.prefer: Ce que j’aime dans ce quartier, c’est le calme.
mistakes.why: The focused element is the object of `aimer`, so the cleft opens with `ce que`; `ce qui` is reserved for a subject.

mistakes.avoid: C’est la bibliothèque que a transformé la vie du quartier.
mistakes.prefer: C’est la bibliothèque qui a transformé la vie du quartier.
mistakes.why: The relative pronoun is the subject of `a transformé`, so use `qui`, not `que`.

mistakes.avoid: La ville doit garantir un air pure et une eau potables à tous les résidents.
mistakes.prefer: La ville doit garantir un air pur et une eau potable à tous les résidents.
mistakes.why: `Air` is masculine singular, so use `pur`; `eau` is feminine singular, so use `potable` without a plural s.

vocabulary.example: Un enjeu environnemental majeur mérite une réponse collective.
vocabulary.note: Masculine noun; stronger than `un problème` in argued writing.

vocabulary.example: La santé mentale des salariés dépend aussi de bonnes conditions de travail.
vocabulary.note: Feminine noun phrase; the gender comes from `santé`.

vocabulary.example: Certes, la mesure est coûteuse, mais elle bénéficie à tout le quartier.
vocabulary.note: Concession frame; the objection comes first, the answer second.

vocabulary.example: Le centre-ville est bien desservi ; en revanche, la périphérie reste isolée.
vocabulary.note: Formal contrast connector; `par contre` is more familiar.

vocabulary.example: Un immigrant récemment arrivé cherche souvent un logement près de son travail.
vocabulary.note: Masculine noun used in Canada; feminine `une immigrante`.

vocabulary.example: Les loyers ont grimpé de douze pour cent en deux ans.
vocabulary.note: Used for a steep rise in figures; `augmenter` is the neutral verb.

vocabulary.example: Le nombre de demandes en attente a baissé depuis la réforme.
vocabulary.note: Intransitive for a fall; transitive in `baisser les prix`.

vocabulary.example: Un quartier solidaire organise des collectes pour les familles touchées.
vocabulary.note: Same form in both genders; `la solidarité` is the related noun.

vocabulary.example: Une émeute a été évitée grâce à la médiation des associations locales.
vocabulary.note: Feminine noun; frequent in news reports and argued texts.

vocabulary.example: Ce qui manque dans ce secteur, c’est une clinique sans rendez-vous.
vocabulary.note: Use `ce que… c’est` instead when the focused element is an object.

vocabulary.example: L’air pur reste un enjeu de santé publique dans les grandes villes.
vocabulary.note: Masculine noun; `l’air clair` would describe brightness, not cleanliness.

vocabulary.example: L’eau potable doit être accessible dans chaque logement locatif.
vocabulary.note: Feminine noun phrase; `l’eau claire` only describes transparency.

vocabulary.example: Un commerce de quartier attire les résidents et crée des emplois locaux.
vocabulary.note: Masculine noun; `le commerce` can name trade in general, while `un commerce` can name a shop or business.

practice.prompt: Write a claim and one supported reason on whether French classes should be free for newcomers.
practice.hint: State the side first, then attach a concrete consequence.
practice.answer: Selon moi, les cours de français devraient rester gratuits pour les nouveaux arrivants. En effet, une meilleure maîtrise de la langue accélère l’accès à l’emploi et réduit l’isolement.

takeaways: Claim, support, concession, conclusion.
Every reason needs a concrete example or consequence.
`Il est important que` and `afin que` take the subjunctive.
`Ce qui` focuses a subject, `ce que` an object, `c’est… qui/que` one phrase.
Clean air is `pur`, drinkable water is `potable`.

modules.title: Les méthodes d’apprentissage
modules.description: Plan a flexible learning sequence, remember nouns with their articles, practise recall, and learn from recurring errors.

lessons.title: Organiser une progression d’apprentissage
lessons.summary: Build a flexible route from useful short sentences to narration and connected opinions. Practise speaking and writing from the beginning; return to articles, verb forms and sentence structure as needed. Use small independent tasks to discover the next useful point to study, rather than waiting to master all grammar.
objectives: Sequence grammar so that each new point rests on a secured one.
Close every stage with an independent production task.
Recognise when a point is secure enough to move on.

sections.title: Core concept
paragraphs: A useful learning sequence connects a small language goal to a real task. Begin with short sentences and noun phrases, such as un petit appartement: an article, an adjective and a noun. Add questions, negation and past tenses when you need to ask for information or describe an experience. Later, develop longer explanations and comparisons. This is a suggested route, not a rule that forbids using a form before you have studied its whole system.

Speak and write at every stage. You can learn Je voudrais savoir… as a useful polite phrase before studying every conditional form. Likewise, you can give a simple opinion with Je préfère… parce que… without knowing the subjunctive. Revisit earlier topics as your sentences become more demanding.

After studying a point, try a small task without the model, then compare and correct it. If you get stuck, identify the actual obstacle: an unknown word, a verb form, a misunderstood instruction or too much new material at once. One difficulty does not show that you must repeat an entire stage. Try the same skill again later; one successful attempt is evidence of progress, not proof of permanent mastery.
The comparisons below correct study beliefs, not French grammar: the crossed-out sentences are grammatically possible.
points: Choose a concrete goal: introduce yourself, ask about a rental, describe an experience or explain a preference.
Learn the words and patterns needed for that goal, including the articles and genders of new nouns.
Move from a model to a changed example, then to a sentence of your own.
Combine new material with earlier skills instead of treating completed lessons as finished forever.
Use mistakes to choose a focused next step, not to abandon the whole task.

examples.french: Je maîtrise d’abord les articles, puis je les réemploie dans une argumentation complète.
examples.english: I first master the articles, then reuse them in a full argument.
examples.note: Each stage feeds the next.

examples.french: Après chaque notion, je réalise une activité guidée puis une tâche autonome.
examples.english: After each concept, I complete a guided activity and then an independent task.
examples.note: Support is gradually withdrawn.

examples.french: Cette semaine, je révise le passé composé ; la semaine prochaine, je raconterai mon installation.
examples.english: This week I revise the compound past; next week I will narrate my arrival.
examples.note: A rule is followed by a real production task.

examples.french: Si je n’arrive pas à rédiger ce courriel sans notes, je repère ce qui me manque.
examples.english: If I cannot write this email without notes, I identify what I am missing.
examples.note: Diagnose a specific gap before deciding what to review.

examples.french: Je cherche un petit appartement près de la gare.
examples.english: I am looking for a small apartment near the station.
examples.note: A first rental task: un appartement (m.), une gare (f.), a present-tense verb and a location.

examples.french: J’ai visité un appartement hier. Il était lumineux, mais le loyer était trop élevé.
examples.english: I visited an apartment yesterday. It was bright, but the rent was too high.
examples.note: Develop the same topic: passé composé for the visit, imparfait for the description, and mais for contrast.

examples.french: Je voudrais savoir si les charges sont comprises.
examples.english: I would like to know whether the service charges are included.
examples.note: A useful polite request you can learn as a whole phrase; si means whether here.

examples.french: Bien que le loyer soit élevé, l’appartement me convient parce qu’il est près de mon travail.
examples.english: Although the rent is high, the apartment suits me because it is near my workplace.
examples.note: A later extension adds a concession with bien que + subjunctive and a reason with parce que.

mistakes.avoid: Je dois maîtriser toute la grammaire avant de commencer à parler.
mistakes.prefer: Je commence à parler avec quelques structures, puis j’élargis ce que je peux exprimer.
mistakes.why: This corrects an unnecessary study restriction, not a grammatical error. Useful communication and grammar study can develop together.

mistakes.avoid: Cette règle me paraît familière, donc je n’ai pas besoin de l’utiliser.
mistakes.prefer: Cette règle me paraît familière ; je l’essaie dans une phrase nouvelle.
mistakes.why: Familiarity alone does not show that you can produce the form. A new sentence gives you something concrete to review.

vocabulary.example: Un apprentissage progressif relie chaque nouvelle notion aux acquis précédents.
vocabulary.note: Masculine noun; the ending -age is a masculine hint.

vocabulary.example: Une progression cohérente mène des bases grammaticales à la production autonome.
vocabulary.note: Feminine noun; the ending -ion is a feminine hint.

vocabulary.example: Une tâche autonome révèle immédiatement les points encore fragiles.
vocabulary.note: Feminine noun; distinct from `un travail`, which is broader.

vocabulary.example: Je maîtrise maintenant l’accord des adjectifs dans mes textes.
vocabulary.note: Regular `-er` verb; `la maîtrise` is the related noun.

practice.prompt: Name the three stages of your own sequence and the task that will close the second one.
practice.hint: Noun phrase, narration and interaction, then complex forms.
practice.answer: D’abord les articles et les accords, ensuite les temps du récit et les pronoms, enfin le subjonctif ; la deuxième étape se terminera par le récit écrit de mon installation.

takeaways: Use a flexible progression from useful sentences to more demanding tasks.
Speak and write at every stage, with decreasing support.
Diagnose the specific obstacle and revisit earlier material when useful.

lessons.title: Mémoriser les noms avec leur déterminant
lessons.summary: Store every French common noun as a complete group: determiner, noun, and an explicit gender or number marker. Use `un` or `une` for a countable noun, a definite article for a concept or a mass noun where that is the natural form, and record plural-only nouns as such. When the gender is uncertain, mark it as uncertain and check it rather than guessing.
objectives: Record a noun in the form you will actually use in a sentence.
Choose the article that matches the noun type.
Handle uncertain genders without guessing.

sections.title: Core concept
paragraphs: Record a reference form with an article and an explicit gender marker: une stratégie (f.), not just the isolated word. Knowing the gender helps you choose agreeing forms such as une nouvelle stratégie. You will still choose the article and number to fit the sentence; the card removes the need to guess the noun’s gender.

For a countable noun, un or une makes the gender visible on the card: un dossier (m.), une demande (f.). For a concept or a mass noun, a definite article can provide a useful reference form: le chômage (m.), la santé (f.), le lait (m.). These are card-writing conventions, not rules for every sentence. You may say un dossier, le dossier or mon dossier depending on what you mean; le lait becomes du lait for an unspecified quantity.

Record a genuinely plural-only meaning as plural: les frais (m. pl.) means fees or expenses. Do not confuse this with a word merely common in the plural. Les céréales (f. pl.) can mean breakfast cereal, but une céréale (f.) also exists for a cereal plant or grain type. Include the relevant meaning on the card.

An elided or plural article does not show gender: l’hôpital (m.), l’université (f.), les vacances (f. pl.). Keep the explicit marker and verify uncertain meanings in a dictionary rather than guessing. The study-habit comparisons below are not corrections of French grammar.
points: Write the determiner and the gender marker on the card itself.
On a reference card, un or une is a convenient gender cue for a countable noun.
A definite article can introduce a concept or mass noun; the article in a sentence still depends on context.
Distinguish a plural-only meaning from an ordinary noun often used in the plural.
Flag an uncertain gender and verify it before reuse.

examples.french: J’ai adopté une stratégie de révision simple et régulière.
examples.english: I have adopted a simple, regular revision strategy.
examples.note: The card `une stratégie (f.)` produces the article and the agreement directly.

examples.french: Un argument illustré par un exemple convainc davantage le lecteur.
examples.english: An argument illustrated by an example is more convincing to the reader.
examples.note: Countable noun stored with « un ».

examples.french: Le chômage des jeunes diminue lentement dans cette région.
examples.english: Youth unemployment is slowly decreasing in this region.
examples.note: A concept stored with the definite article.

examples.french: Des frais de dossier s’appliquent après la date limite.
examples.english: File processing fees apply after the deadline.
examples.note: The fees/expenses meaning is plural-only: les frais (m. pl.).

examples.french: Le blé est une céréale.
examples.english: Wheat is a cereal crop.
examples.note: Une céréale (f.) is a valid singular noun. Frequent plural use does not make it plural-only.

examples.french: J’achète des céréales pour le petit-déjeuner.
examples.english: I buy breakfast cereal.
examples.note: In this food context French commonly uses the plural; English often treats cereal as a mass noun.

examples.french: Le lait est dans le réfrigérateur. Je voudrais du lait, s’il vous plaît.
examples.english: The milk is in the fridge. I would like some milk, please.
examples.note: The reference form le lait (m.) gives gender; du lait expresses an unspecified quantity.

mistakes.avoid: Je note « stratégie » dans mon carnet et je choisis l’article au moment d’écrire.
mistakes.prefer: Je note « une stratégie (f.) » et je réutilise le groupe complet.
mistakes.why: Deciding the article each time reproduces the same hesitation and the same agreement errors.

mistakes.avoid: Je devine le genre d’un mot nouveau et je l’emploie immédiatement.
mistakes.prefer: Je marque le genre comme incertain, je le vérifie, puis je l’emploie.
mistakes.why: A guessed gender that is practised becomes a habit that is hard to correct later.

vocabulary.example: Une stratégie de révision espacée améliore la mémorisation à long terme.
vocabulary.note: Feminine noun; stored with its article on the card.

vocabulary.example: Un exemple concret rend un argument beaucoup plus convaincant.
vocabulary.note: Masculine noun; `par exemple` is the fixed adverbial phrase.

vocabulary.example: Le chômage recule lentement dans les grandes villes.
vocabulary.note: Masculine mass noun; naturally stored with the definite article.

vocabulary.example: Une fiche complète comprend le déterminant, le nom et le genre.
vocabulary.note: Feminine noun; `une fiche de vocabulaire` is a vocabulary card.

practice.prompt: Write vocabulary cards for `travail`, `santé`, and `frais` in the required format.
practice.hint: Countable, mass noun, plural-only.
practice.answer: un travail (m.), la santé (f.), les frais (m. pl.)

takeaways: Determiner, noun, gender and meaning belong together on a card.
A reference article identifies gender; sentence context determines the article you actually use.
Never practise a guessed gender.

lessons.title: La récupération active et la révision espacée
lessons.summary: Try to retrieve an answer before revealing it, then use feedback and delayed review. Adapt review dates to difficulty rather than treating one schedule as compulsory. Include recognition, production and correction, with new sentences as well as familiar examples.
objectives: Retrieve before checking, on every item.
Space the intervals according to how secure the item is.
Alternate recognition, production, and correction.

sections.title: Core concept
paragraphs: Active recall means trying to retrieve an answer from memory before revealing the answer or model. You can see a question or cue; it is the answer that stays hidden. For example, look at the cue Say: I am going to the market, produce the French, then check Je vais au marché. Rereading can help you understand a point, but familiarity with a visible answer is not the same as retrieving it.

Spaced review puts a delay between attempts. One starting schedule is a review tomorrow, another three days from today, then one week and one month from today. These dates are examples, not a universally optimal timetable. Adjust for difficulty, your study opportunities and how long you need to retain the material. After a wrong answer, read the explanation and retry with a short gap; revisit it later rather than repeatedly guessing.

Vary the demand: recognise a form in a text, produce it from a cue, and explain a correction. Recognition alone does not show that you can produce the form, so include sentences of your own. The comparisons below discuss study habits; they do not label grammatical French as incorrect.
points: Hide the answer, restate the rule aloud, then check.
Write one new sentence rather than repeating the example on the card.
Lengthen the interval after an easy recall and shorten it after a failure.
Correct a failed attempt, retry after a short gap, then schedule another review.
Alternate recognition, production, and correction across sessions.

examples.french: Je ferme la fiche, puis je reformule la règle avec mes propres mots.
examples.english: I close the card, then restate the rule in my own words.
examples.note: The retrieval step, before any checking.

examples.french: Je révise cette règle demain, puis dans trois jours et dans une semaine.
examples.english: I review this rule tomorrow, then in three days and in one week.
examples.note: Intervals that grow as the item becomes secure.

examples.french: J’écris une phrase nouvelle au lieu de recopier l’exemple de la fiche.
examples.english: I write a new sentence instead of copying the example from the card.
examples.note: Production rather than recognition.

examples.french: Cette règle m’a résisté hier, alors je la revois dès ce soir.
examples.english: This rule gave me trouble yesterday, so I am reviewing it again this evening.
examples.note: A difficult item gets another attempt rather than being left until a distant fixed date.

examples.french: Je vais au marché.
examples.english: I am going to the market.
examples.note: Cue: say I am going to the market. Hide this answer first; then check vais and the contraction à + le → au.

examples.french: Elle va au bureau demain.
examples.english: She is going to the office tomorrow.
examples.note: Transfer the pattern to a new subject and place instead of reciting the first sentence.

examples.french: J’utilise une nouvelle stratégie.
examples.english: I am using a new strategy.
examples.note: Cue: produce this message from the English, without looking. Check une stratégie (f.) and feminine nouvelle, then try a different context.

mistakes.avoid: Je relis la même fiche trois fois, puis je passe à la suivante.
mistakes.prefer: Je masque la réponse, je la retrouve de mémoire, puis je vérifie.
mistakes.why: Both sentences are grammatical. The second study routine adds a retrieval attempt, which rereading alone does not provide.

mistakes.avoid: Je révise toutes mes fiches au même rythme, les faciles comme les difficiles.
mistakes.prefer: J’espace davantage les fiches sûres et je ramène rapidement les fiches difficiles.
mistakes.why: Adapting review frequency can give difficult items more attention. A fixed schedule can still be a useful starting point.

vocabulary.example: La récupération active oblige l’apprenant à retrouver une réponse sans consulter la fiche.
vocabulary.note: Feminine noun phrase; the gender comes from `récupération`.

vocabulary.example: Une révision espacée revient au moment où le souvenir commence à s’affaiblir.
vocabulary.note: Feminine noun phrase; the gender comes from `révision`.

vocabulary.example: Je reformule la règle avec mes propres mots avant de vérifier.
vocabulary.note: Regular `-er` verb; central to the recall step.

vocabulary.example: Un intervalle plus long convient à une fiche déjà bien retenue.
vocabulary.note: Masculine noun despite its final -e.

practice.prompt: Describe your next three review dates for a rule you found difficult today.
practice.hint: A failed item returns sooner than a secure one.
practice.answer: Je la revois ce soir, puis demain, puis dans trois jours si la récupération est réussie.

takeaways: Retrieve first, check second.
Intervals grow with security and shrink after a failure.
Recognise, produce, correct: three modes, not one.

lessons.title: Le carnet d’erreurs et la boucle de correction
lessons.summary: An error log records four things for each recurring error: the wrong sentence, the corrected sentence, the rule in one line, and a new sentence written without the model. Classify errors by category — gender and agreement, tense and mood, prepositions and verb complements, word choice, register — so that patterns become visible and can be targeted.
objectives: Classify each error into a stable category.
State the correcting rule in a single line.
Close the loop with a new sentence written without the model.

sections.title: Core concept
paragraphs: An error log records mistakes worth revisiting, especially recurring ones or those that change your meaning. Useful categories include gender and agreement, tense and mood, prepositions and verb complements, word choice, and register. Add spelling, punctuation, word order or pronunciation when needed; these categories are tools, not an exhaustive list you must fit every error into.

Use four steps: record the original sentence, find a reliable correction, explain the relevant rule or meaning difference, then write a new sentence without the model. A new example tests whether you can transfer the point rather than merely recognise the corrected sentence. Revisit it later. You do not need to log every accidental typo or count every mistake to benefit.

For example, if you wrote J’ai allé à la clinique, the problem is the auxiliary of aller in the passé composé. The correction is Je suis allé à la clinique, or allée when the speaker uses feminine agreement. The useful rule is: aller takes être here, and its past participle agrees with the subject. Then change the message and subject: Ma sœur est allée à la pharmacie.

A correction may instead concern meaning or register. A grammatical sentence is not automatically suitable for every situation. In the study-habit comparisons below, the French itself is grammatical; the proposed improvement is the way you use feedback.
points: Choose a recurring or important error and give it a useful category.
Keep both versions: what you wrote and what is correct.
Write a short explanation you understand, including an exception or context when it matters.
Produce a new sentence on a different topic, without the model.
Review the log regularly and choose one pattern to practise next; totals are optional.

examples.french: Je classe cette erreur dans la catégorie « accord du participe passé », puis je réécris la phrase.
examples.english: I file this error under the category “past-participle agreement”, then I rewrite the sentence.
examples.note: Classification comes before correction.

examples.french: J’écris la correction, puis je crée une nouvelle phrase sans consulter le modèle.
examples.english: I write the correction, then create a new sentence without consulting the model.
examples.note: The transfer step that closes the loop.

examples.french: Après la correction, je réemploie la règle dans un nouvel argument.
examples.english: After the correction, I reuse the rule in a new argument.
examples.note: Transfer into a different type of text.

examples.french: Cette semaine, huit erreurs sur douze concernaient les prépositions.
examples.english: This week, eight errors out of twelve involved prepositions.
examples.note: A count can help reveal a pattern, but a frequent error is not necessarily the most serious one.

examples.french: Je suis allée à la clinique hier.
examples.english: I went to the clinic yesterday.
examples.note: Corrected model for a speaker using feminine agreement: suis, not ai; allée, not allé.

examples.french: Ma sœur est allée à la pharmacie.
examples.english: My sister went to the pharmacy.
examples.note: Transfer the same rule to a new subject and destination: elle est allée.

examples.french: Nous sommes allés à la bibliothèque.
examples.english: We went to the library.
examples.note: Transfer to plural nous: allés for a masculine or mixed group, allées for a group using feminine agreement.

mistakes.avoid: Je copie la correction dans mon carnet et je passe à l’exercice suivant.
mistakes.prefer: J’écris la correction, je justifie la règle en une ligne, puis je rédige une phrase nouvelle.
mistakes.why: Both sentences are grammatical. The second method includes an explanation and a transfer attempt; copying alone does not show that you can produce the form.

mistakes.avoid: Je note toutes mes erreurs dans une seule liste, sans catégorie.
mistakes.prefer: Je classe chaque erreur par catégorie et je compte les occurrences chaque semaine.
mistakes.why: Categories can make recurring patterns easier to notice. A simple list can also be useful; weekly counting is optional, not a condition for learning.

vocabulary.example: Un carnet d’erreurs rassemble les corrections qui méritent une nouvelle mise en pratique.
vocabulary.note: Masculine noun phrase; the gender comes from `carnet`.

vocabulary.example: Une rétroaction précise explique la correction et indique comment progresser.
vocabulary.note: Feminine noun; standard term in Canada, where `un retour` is more general.

vocabulary.example: Une catégorie bien choisie révèle immédiatement les erreurs répétées.
vocabulary.note: Feminine noun; the ending -ie is a feminine hint.

vocabulary.example: Je réemploie la règle corrigée dans un texte différent.
vocabulary.note: `-yer` verb: `j’emploie`, `nous employons`.

practice.prompt: Take the error « J’ai allé à la clinique » and complete the four steps of the loop.
practice.hint: Category, correction, one-line rule, new sentence.
practice.answer: Catégorie : auxiliaire du passé composé. Correction : « Je suis allé à la clinique. » Règle : « aller » se conjugue avec « être » et le participe s’accorde avec le sujet. Nouvelle phrase : « Elle est arrivée au centre communautaire à neuf heures. »

takeaways: Use categories that fit your recurring errors; add or simplify them as needed.
Four steps: wrong, right, rule, new sentence.
Without the transfer step the loop is not closed.
